Emotes.text:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:'''Emotes'''}} ==What Are Emotes?== [[File:EmoteOption.png|300px|right|thumb|'''The emote option in the shop.''']] Emotes are cosmetic taunts/dances that can be used for shenanigans. While performing an emote, your character will play an animation (often with sound and/or visual effects) that lasts until the emote ends. You can cancel an emote early by jumping, attacking (M1), blocking, or getting hit. An emote can fall into seven categories: *'''Stationary''': Keeps the user in a fixed spot/lowers their movement speed by a great amount. *'''Cosmetic''': Applies effects on the user that last after the emote ends. These effects will be removed upon death, and in some cases, if the emote is reused. *'''Traversal''': Allows (or forces) the user to move at a certain speed while performed. *'''Partner''': Allows other players to join in and emote along the user via an interaction prompt. **'''Duo''' emotes only allow one player to interact with the user at a time. **'''Group''' emotes allow an infinite amount of players to interact with the user. *'''Kill''': Interacts with dead players, and can cause death in particular cases. *'''Interactive''': Comes with an action button, a space for typing, or special controls. *'''Limited/Exclusive''': Can only be obtained with means other than the shop (redeeming a [[Codes|code]], participating in an [[Events|event]], finding secrets..). ===Obtaining=== [[File:Ten Emote Menu.png|right|150px]] An emote can be obtained from the [[Shop]] at a random indicated chance at the price of $250 or 25 {{Robux}}, with a multiplier option that allows you to buy 5 or 10 emotes at once. Getting 10 emotes at once will let you pick the 10th emote from a list of all the unexclusive emotes, with the option to postpone this action to the next time you join the game by pressing "Pick Later". Emotes can also be gifted to other players using {{Robux}} by selecting the "Gifting" tab, and scrolling down to the emote options.
As of now, the game features 413 purchasable emotes (costing a total of $103250 or 10325 {{Robux}}) and 42 exclusive emotes.
Players in regions with anti-gambling laws (such as the UK, Australia or Brazil) cannot use {{Robux}} to roll for emotes. ===Equipping=== Once obtained, emotes will be sorted from newest to oldest in the inventory (alphabetical sorting is available as well) where they can be placed onto the emote wheel. [[File:EmoteWheel.png|link=|frameless|right|50px]] To access the emote wheel, press the dancing person icon or '''B''' on PC. This will also pull up [[Kogane]] to the right of the wheel. ===[[Gamepasses]]=== Owning the '''[[Gamepasses#More Emote Slots|More Emote Slots]]''' gamepass will add 4 extra slots to the corners of the emote wheel, increasing the number of emotes that can be placed at a time from 4 to 8. For every '''[[Gamepasses#+1 Emote Page|+1 Emote Page]]''' gamepass, a new page will be added to the emote wheel, with 4 empty slots along with a search bar above the wheel that permits the user to perform an emote without equipping it. This makes certain emotes occupy large parts of the map if used with {{Puppet Master}}'s Absolute. *It is possible to clip into domains using 'Bow3', 'Garbage', 'Clash1,' ‘Looping’, 'Tired', 'Flop', and 'A Mimir?', 'Brightest Heart', 'Absolute Cinema', 'Bow2', 'King of Curses'. You'll need to stick to the domain border (face it if you're planning on using 'Garbage', 'A Mimir?' or 'Tired', or face 90 degrees to the side using ‘Looping’, and face away if you're using 'Bow3'), use the emote, turn off Shiftlock and direct yourself to the opposite direction before canceling the emote. **You can also do that with the 'Stylish' emote, having your left arm stick out of the domain, and waiting for the part where you go sideways, then activate shiftlock to get inside. It is more recommended to use other emotes, since the part that you can get in the domain takes time to appear. **The 'Places' emote can be used to glitch a player through domain borders by turning around to face the domain once someone interacts with you. (It is actually possible to send both you and the other player into the domain, though once the domain ends there's a 50/50 chance you get voided or teleported near the edges so beware). **You can also do that with the 'Turron' emote, facing away from the domain use the emote, wait till you go forward, then shiftlock facing the domain and cancel the emote. You can bring another player using this emote into a domain too. **The 'Flop' emote can be used to clip into a domain as well. To enter a domain, press against the border while facing it and use the emote. Once you flop onto the ground once, jump before you get up and you should be in the domain, if not simply do it until you succeed. *Due to the {{Honored One}}'s Infinite Void only preventing active movement and actions, activating a moving emote before being affected by the domain will allow you to move inside the domain until the emote is interrupted. This also applies to the starting animation of {{Restless Gambler}}'s domain but does not apply to 0.2 Domain. *The emote "Drag" can be used to fly in the air by flicking your camera around when dragging a person. *While it seems that you can't move during stationary emotes, you are able to, as stationary emotes set your walking speed to a very low value instead of 0. Using Flight in a Private Server will make the movement quicker as you gain speed the longer you move without stopping. *Ignoring the visual effects, the 'Lying Rage' and 'Stomp' emote actually have the exact same animation. *All animations of Limited/Exclusive emotes are inaccessible within the Animation mode in [[Build Mode/Skill Builder|Skill Builder]]. *There's a funny glitch involving the 'Jeep' emote, where if you position the dummy on the indented part of the jeep, you can fly upwards *While {{Head of the Hei}} is stuck in their frame, they can continue moving with the 'Jeep' emote __NOTOC__

Domain Expansion.text:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:'''DOMAIN EXPANSION'''}} A '''Domain Expansion''' (or "領域展開" [romanized as ''Ryōiki Tenkai'']) is a move category in ''Jujutsu Shenanigans'' that; after a short handsign windup, expands the character's domain, which is a large destructible dome that can either have a white or black border. The inner part of the dome features a unique environment with the user's cursed technique embedded into it, which imbues most of the domains with a sure-hit property during its '''''full''''' active period. ----
  • Domains
  • Domain
    Clashes
  • Anti
    Domains
  • Border
    Breaking
  • VSFX
Expanding a domain generally takes 1.25 seconds (exceptions being '''Embodiment of Self Perfection''' and '''Authentic Mutual Love''', both expanding in 1.5 seconds) and causes a pop-up to appear for all players within the domain's range (generally being a 37.5 stud radius). However, domains have several casting conditions that prohibit their expansion in certain situations: *Domains cannot be opened while inside another domain or too close to its border, nor can they be cast while the user is airborne. *If multiple domains are cast at the same time or within a short window, a Domain Clash will ensue to determine the domain to trump the others. **Domains can also be cast during the Awakening sequence in case the user was caught in range of one. *If hit or stunned while expanding a domain, the entire domain will be canceled. Few domains grant total immunity during their windups, which excludes them from this requirement. {|class="fandom-table" !Domain !Time !Description |- |style="text-align: center;" | [[File:InfiniteVoid.gif|frameless|250px]]
'''{{Honored One}}: Infinite Void''' |14s |The inner part of the domain resembles a blue void with stars/galaxies shining around it. Endless information begins flooding the minds of everyone inside but the user, making them completely unable to act for 14 seconds. The sure-hit won't interrupt any actions however, meaning enemies can keep moving around or attacking if they were performing an action before the domain's effect applied. |- |style="text-align: center;" | [[File:0.2Domain.gif|frameless|250px]]
'''{{Honored One}}: 0.2 Domain''' |7s |By using the special during the Awakening sequence, the player activates an ‘Alternate Awakening’ and immediately expands Infinite Void after taking their blindfold off, but only for two-tenths of a second. This distributes the domain’s sure-hit effect over double the normal range, at the cost of exposing targets to it for only half the usual duration. Right after the windup, the user prepares a deadly rush with unbelievable speeds and relentless strikes, split into 3 phases. |- |style="text-align: center;" | [[File:MalevolentShrine.gif|frameless|250px]]
'''{{Vessel}}: Malevolent Shrine''' |12s |When cast, a shrine will be placed behind the user, while the rest of the domain remains a black void with red smoke on the horizon. Everyone within the domain will be hit with slashes constantly, with each slash dealing 2 HP, totaling 156 HP for 78 slashes. Blocking will reduce the damage of the slashes to 0.5 HP and prevent them from executing. |- |style="text-align: center;" | [[File:IdleDeathGamble.gif|frameless|250px]]
'''{{Restless Gambler}}: Idle Death Gamble''' |80s |Upon awakening, the user will perform a handsign to cast their domain, Idle Death Gamble, as they gain total invincibility. Once successfully opened, everyone caught inside the domain will be frozen in place as they are set into a neutral stage while rainbow text appears at the top left of their screens, detailing the domain's mechanics. The user's goal is to gamble by rolling for jackpot through Richii scenarios. To progress the stage to a Richii scenario, the caster must perform 2 visual moves, which count as: * Using Reserve Balls. * Using Shutter Doors. ** Using Reserve Balls and Shutter Doors' combination will count as 2 visual moves. * Landing Fever Breaker's dropkick. ** Fever Crush will count as one visual move. * A successful Door Guard. Once a Richii scenario is triggered, its success will dictate whether jackpot is awarded: ---- '''Transit Card Richii (☆☆★)''' * In this scenario, Tze is walking towards a train checkpoint. If Tze passes through the train checkpoint, the user will enter the Jackpot state. If Tze flies upward, the user must retry. ---- '''Travel Emergency Richii (☆★★)''' *In this scenario, Tze is running to the male bathroom. If Tze goes in, the user will enter their Jackpot state. If Tze falls, the user must retry. ---- The user has only 4 attempts to reach the jackpot before the domain breaks, but on the 4th roll, they are guaranteed to obtain a "pity" jackpot with half the usual Awakening period if at least one player was caught in the domain. After each roll, numbered symbols will appear on every player's screen. On a successful roll, and depending on the category of the integers, a jackpot bonus comes into play: *If the numbers were odd, such as 777, their next Idle Death Gamble will feature an increased chance of a jackpot. *If the numbers were even, such as 666, their next Idle Death Gamble will feature faster Richii scenarios. Note that death takes away these bonuses. |- |style="text-align: center;" | [[File:SelfEmbodimentofPerfection.gif|frameless|250px]]
'''{{Perfection}}: Embodiment of Self Perfection''' |14s |The user looks up and transfigures several tiny arms in their mouth to form their domain's hand sign. The inner part of the domain consists of an empty void with hands forming a flower-like pattern.
All targets caught within get a "transfiguration meter" to their right side, which will deplete when near the domain caster. The drain will speed up when taking damage from the caster's attack while in range, and once the bar is empty, the target will take severe damage over time, equaling to 3 times their maximum health every tick, before their body transfigures and explodes to bits. |- |style="text-align: center;" | [[File:Deadly Sentencing.gif|frameless|250px]]
'''{{Defense Attorney}}: Deadly Sentencing''' |300s |Upon activating their Awakening, the user will expand their domain, Deadly Sentencing, which resembles a platform with 2 podiums surrounded by suspended guillotines with the user's shikigami, Judgeman, staying near the caster at all times. Awakening drain and regeneration are both halted, and everyone is invulnerable.
A random accusation sits the top center of the screen above a Judgment Bar split into 3 segments, all while 3 choices appear above everybody's Awakening Bar: "''Confess''", "''Silence''", and "''Denial''".
After the prosecutor picks a choice, a 3 second timer (only visible to them) will begin counting down. If a defendant on the other side doesn’t answer within this timeframe, then "''Silence''" will be chosen for them. If more than one person are against the user, then the deciding choice will be the one picked by the majority of the defendants.
Matching choices fill one segment of the Judgment Bar (except "''Confess''", which instantly fills all three), but a total of six opposing choices will immediately end the trial, indicated by the fallen guillotines. As the caster can willingly close their domain at any point using their Awakening button, the following outcomes can occur from the domain's collapse: *[□□□] '''Innocence''': The domain caster gains 60% of their Awakening back. This also will happen if the user fails to catch anyone within Deadly Sentencing. ---- *[■□□] '''Confiscation''': Everyone inside the domain will temporarily lose access to their held item or 2 random abilities for 1 minute and 30 seconds, while the user regains 40% of their Awakening and 60% of their health back. **Note that Confiscation carries over to Awakenings, meaning any Awakening moves on confiscated slots will be taken away until the 90 seconds pass. **Items are confiscated permanently. ---- *[■■□] '''Death Penalty''': The caster's gavel will break into pieces to reveal the Executioner's Sword, their true Awakening. If the caster reaches their Awakening this way, then the Awakening duration will be 30 seconds longer. **Note that all defendants will be stunned during the Awakening sequence. ---- *[■■■] '''Confiscation + Death Penalty''': The domain will immediately break with everyone losing a random ability for 90 seconds or their held item, while the caster gains access to the Executioner's Sword and 60% of their health back. **As usual, all defendants will be stunned during the Awakening sequence, Confiscation carries over to Awakenings until the 90 seconds period ends, and items are confiscated permanently. |- |style="text-align: center;" | [[File:AuthenticMutualLove.gif|frameless|250px]]
'''{{Cursed Partners}}: Authentic Mutual Love''' |45s |The user casts their Domain Expansion, conjuring a stone platform with several structures rising from the ground, and knots symbolizing their love circling the sky. Several blades rain down from above, though only four land within reach, all imbued with a random technique out of the following: Shrine, Thin Ice Breaker, Clairvoyance, Cursed Speech, and Shikigami. By standing near a blade, the user can equip it then perform a long run ending with a swing that activates the technique. After each pickup, another blade falls. This domain breaks immediately if no enemies are within.
After landing 4 katanas, the user can conjure Jacob's Ladder from the sky by using their domain again with a target in sight, which will catch that target and slowly lift them up while draining their health and 35% of their Awakening progress (50% if they are awakened). This grants total i-frames to the user during the windup while bypassing all others, but takes a toll on the domain and shatters it immediately. The current progress towards unlocking Jacob's Ladder is shown on the domain's skill box if no katana is held.
*If you wish to know each of the domain katanas' effects, click [[Cursed Partners#Authentic_Mutual_Love|this highlighted link]]. |- |style="text-align: center;" | [[File:TimeCellMoonPalace.gif|frameless|250px]]
'''{{Head of the Hei}}: Time Cell Moon Palace''' |25s |Hopping out of their curse form, the user performs a handsign to expand their innate domain, Time Cell Moon Palace, while reverting back to their base moveset with the same HP percentage. Their cursed technique is additionally amplified in many ways: *As rolls of film are injected into the neck of every opponent caught within the domain, they are forced to abide by Projection Sorcery's 24 FPS rule at all times, which now operates on a cellular level. This means that any movement or action will result their cells freezing in frames then shattering, including ragdoll and wakeup. **Blocking is excluded, and will significantly reduce the damage from walking. *Failing to land moves will add no projection to the user's own meter. |- |style="text-align: center;" | [[File:ShiningSeaofGrowingBranches.gif|frameless|250px]]
'''{{Disaster Plants}}: Shining Sea of Growing Branches''' |15s |The user casts their domain expansion while kneeling on the ground to sap energy from nearby foliage. The inner part of the domain resembles a large bed of flowers with distant trees, where any action other than running, side dashing or blocking will get interrupted and punish its perpetrator with stun and damage. The user also gains a significant boost from both their domain and their earlier absorption, putting their Flower Beam off cooldown while boosting it and remaining empowered for the entire duration of the domain. |- |style="text-align: center;" | [[File:IncompleteShrine.gif|frameless|250px]]
'''{{Strongest Of History}}: Incomplete Shrine''' |20s |Upon initiating their Awakening, the user expands the impromptu variation of Malevolent Shrine without enclosing a barrier with a shell, creating bigger version of the original shrine, with 9 eyes and a giant mouth. Similarly to its previous version, the domain's sure-hit effect will send relentless slashes to rip everything apart, dealing 375 HP (75 HP with block) worth of slashes, with each slash dealing 3 HP, and 0.6 HP when blocked. The destruction range however, is limited. |}
Several abilities have functions made directly to counter Domain Expansions in different ways; although some domains, such as 0.2 Domain and Incomplete Shrine, are immune as they lack proper borders. {|class="fandom-table" !Ability !Description |- | style="text-align: center;" |[[File:ChimeraShadowGarden.gif|frameless|250px]]
'''Chimera Shadow Garden''' |When using Shadow Swarm against a domain border, the user lays out their own domain; “Chimera Shadow Garden”, to clash with the targeted domain and invade it through a hole in the twisting shadows. As long as this ability is active, all players are free to enter or leave the invaded domain, excluding the user who will remain in place as their health bar depletes due to the strain of maintaining the portal, until it is closed by either using Shadow Swarm again, getting hit, or having no health left to spare.
The following sure-hit effects will be disabled while Chimera Shadow Garden is active: *Infinite Void's stun. *Malevolent Shrine's slashes. *Embodiment Of Self-Perfection's transfiguration bar drain. *Time Cell Moon Palace's frame shatter. *Shining Sea of Growing Branches' interruption.

'''Domain Amplification''' |When using their special, the user covers themselves with a thin veil of their own domain expansion around them, which will protect them from the sure-hit effect of any domain expansion they are within unless they are hit by anything else, upon which the veil will dissipate and grant them half a second of total i-frames. |- | style="text-align: center;" |[[File:TechniqueCharge.gif|frameless|250px]]
'''Technique Charge:''' '''Simple Domain''' |Using one year's worth of cursed energy, the user deploys a technique-imbued projectile from a compartment in their mech's index finger. The bullet's efficiency improves with every level of Energy Output, especially on the fifth level, where it is imbued with a Simple Domain charge, triggering a secondary impact that ragdolls the target upwards as any active domain expansions immediately shatter. |- | style="text-align: center;" |[[File:Invasion.gif|frameless|250px]]
'''Invasion''' |If Parthenogenesis is activated near a domain border, the user will dedicate a swarm of roaches towards making a hole in the dome that the user will then enter through. Right after, they will remain in a pose while even more pests proceed to chip away at the invaded domain's border to reduce its lifetime by up to 75%.
Note that the hole can be used by any other player who wishes to enter the domain, and the user is not immune to any sure-hit effects while inside but 60% of their Awakening will be refunded once the invasion ends. |}
A Domain Clash occurs when two or more players simultaneously cast their domain expansions. Once a clash is initiated, all expanded domains lose their sure-hit effects and mix into one, disabling Awakening drain along with the abilities of all players while overriding their M1s and dashes with passives similar to {{Head of the Hei}}'s, although all of their M1s cannot stun or ragdoll opponents.

Additionally, all domain contestants will be highlighted and fitted with a bar under them, which fills by 6.25% when landing a hit on an opposing domain caster (non-contestants will add no progress to the bar, although they are still able to participate in the brawl). This means that the bar will fill after 16 landed hits (or 4 M1 sets). The player to fill their bar to its maximum or yield the highest bar percentage at the end of the 15 second timer will win the Domain Clash and cancel all other domains in favor of their own. If all players have the same progress on their bars when the 15-second timer is up, all domains will break. To make up for lethal domains offering immediate advantages to their casters, winning a domain clash will bestow specific bonuses to the following non-lethal domains: *In the case of '''Idle Death Gamble''', the domain will skip its first Richii scenario and immediately grant a jackpot lasting for 100 seconds. *In the case of '''Deadly Sentencing''', the domain will start with a pre-filled segment of its Judgement Bar, making Confiscation its lightest sentence. *Both domains will also refund 75% of the Awakening Bar back to their caster if they are to lose the domain clash. Note that '''0.2 Domain''' and '''Chimera Shadow Garden''' cannot clash with other domains, while '''Incomplete Shrine''' will instantly break all other active domains within its range.
Including the final M1, some moves that cause terrain or ground destruction can damage domains on the outside if they land on its border, making an audible bang noise. As domains cannot be damaged from the inside, killing the caster becomes the only way to destroy it, or in the case of {{Puppet Master}}, hitting the caster with Technique Charge on its maximum Energy Output level. ==Trivia== *In a Domain Clash, held items can override the special M1s. While some (such as Playful Cloud) allow basic attacks to stun, no hits at all can grant bar progress, which causes the user's loss in case they don't get rid of the item before the timer ends. *Although Ryu Ishigori, Yuki Tsukumo and Takako Uro do possess the ability to expand their domains, they were never properly shown off in the ''Jujutsu Kaisen'' series. The same could be said about Hanami, although the character's domain was shown on the mobile game ''Jujutsu Kaisen: Phantom Parade'', and was eventually added into {{Disaster Plants}}'s awakened moveset. **Despite Megumi Fushiguro being able to expand his domain and successfully doing so in the ''Jujutsu Kaisen'' series, it's incomplete nature makes it difficult to add into the game for technical and balancing limitations, so it was excluded. *Adaptation only counts '''Malevolent Shrine''', '''Time Cell Moon Palace''', and '''Incomplete Shrine''' as "Domain Attacks". However, '''Infinite Void''' and '''Shining Sea of Growing Branches''' are also adaptable, but doing so will put Adaptation on a 15 second cooldown without granting any healing nor Ritual progress. On top of that, the adaptation will only last as long as the domain does, meaning those domains must be adapted to whenever caught within. *By placing a spawn in a domain with [[Build Mode|Free Build]], then dying and respawning on it, you're able to customize the inner part of the domain. This is because every domain model spawns at one location far from the map; to prevent domains overlapping, every domain will spawn at a certain distance from the last. Every player inside a domain shell is teleported to that location relative to the caster's position. *Domain borders can either be black or white, depending on which one was used. However, in the case of a domain clash, the border will always be black even after a white-bordered domain wins. **The only domains with white borders are {{Honored One}}'s [[Honored One#Awakening|'''Infinite Void''']] and {{Restless Gambler}}'s [[Restless Gambler#Domain Awakening|'''Idle Death Gamble''']]. **{{Defense Attorney}}'s [[Defense Attorney#Domain Awakening|'''Deadly Sentencing''']] used to be included, but it was changed to black after its redesign. __NOTOC__

Gamepasses.text:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:'''Gamepasses'''}} '''Gamepasses''' are products purchasable only with {{Robux}}, that can be used to improve your gameplay experience. No gamepass (other than [[Gamepasses#Early_Access|Early Access]]) affects your battles. Gamepasses can either be bought or gifted by anyone from the [[Shop]]. Alternatively, they're purchasable directly from the Roblox page. Buying all the gamepasses costs 950 {{Robux}}, without accounting for regional pricing. ---- ==List of Gamepasses==
  • Early
    Access
  • Custom Kill
    Sound
  • More Emote
    Slots
  • Awakening
    Outfits
  • +1 Emote Page
  • More Build
    Saves
{{Gamepass |title1= Early Access |image1= NoFilter.png|Icon |cost={{Robux}} 345 |description=Gives access to incomplete characters}} ====Info==== The '''Early Access''' gamepass allows players to use in-development movesets of unreleased characters. ====Trivia/Notes==== *This gamepass is permanent. You will automatically have access to any and all future in-development movesets. *You may notice bugs or glitches when using Early Access characters, as they are still in development. *13 characters have been in Early Access: {{Restless Gambler}}, {{Ten Shadows}}, {{Perfection}}, {{Blood Manipulator}}, {{Switcher}}, {{Defense Attorney}}, {{Cursed Partners}}, {{Puppet Master}}, {{Head of the Hei}}, {{Salaryman}}, {{Crow Charmer}}, {{Disaster Plants}}, {{True Cannon}}, {{Register}} and {{Sky Bender}}. *Currently, the only character in Early Access is {{Hired Hunter}}. *[[Characters#Base Only|Base-only characters]] and [[Characters#Overpowered|Overpowered characters]] are usually automatically free to the public, with the exceptions of {{Crow Charmer}} and {{Sky Bender}}.
{{Gamepass |title1=Custom Kill Sound |image1= Kill sounds?.png|Icon |cost={{Robux}} 100 |description=Customize the sound that plays when you finish a player}} ====Info==== The '''Custom Kill Sound''' gamepass will unlock 2 new [[Settings#Audio|audio settings]], permitting users to input the ID of the sounds they wish to play when they die and when they kill a player. ====Notes & Trivia==== *If you want to get an audio for your kill sound, you'll have to search in the [https://create.roblox.com/store/audio Roblox Marketplace's] audio section and get the ID you want by copying and pasting it. An audio's ID can be found in the URL, typically as a 10-digit string of numbers. *A custom sound will stop when the dead body it plays from has despawned, which takes about 4 seconds. *Custom sounds can be globally turned off from the in-game [[settings]]. *Newly created sounds, even if distributed to the creator store, tend to not work in Jujutsu Shenanigans, giving the error: "User is not authorized to access Asset." **To identify a newly created sound, check if the ID is unusually long, ROBLOX changed their asset creation system to avoid asset stealing. This means that assets are no longer given an ID based on when they were created and are instead randomized.
{{Gamepass |title1=More Emote Slots |image1=More emote slots.png |cost={{Robux}} 150 |description=Adds 4 more slots to the equip emotes to the emote wheel}} ====Info==== The '''More Emote Slots''' gamepass adds 4 more slots to the emote wheel, giving users a total of 8 emote slots. ====Notes & Trivia==== *This gamepass works simultaneously with the [[Gamepasses#+1 Emote_Page|+1 Emote Page]] gamepass, giving 4 extra slots to every new page.
{{Gamepass |title1=Awakening Outfits |image1= AWK OUTFITS.png|Gamepass GojoAwakeningOutfit.gif|Demonstration |cost={{Robux}} 100 |description=Change your look while you are awakened (generally) }} ====Info==== The '''Awakening Outfits''' add the option to let you switch to a saved Roblox outfit (from the Roblox Avatar Customizer) whenever you activate your Awakening. ====Notes==== *For {{Perfection}}, the player will only equip their Awakening Outfit once they trigger their Super Awakening, not regular Awakening. On top of that, the gauntlets for Perfection's Super Awakening will change to the avatar's skin tone. *For {{Switcher}}, the player's avatar won't change. Instead, the Idol's avatar will change from Tzekada-chan to the selected awakening outfit. *For {{Puppet Master}}, the player's avatar will always consist of the same Mechamaru Mode: Absolute outfit, while Offload's cursed corpses will be the ones using the selected Awakening Outfit. *For {{Head of the Hei}}, the player will first switch to their Awakening Outfit during Vengeance's sequence for a split second before morphing into their cursed spirit form, with its tendrils (legs and arms) always being red and its shell sharing the same color of the Awakening Outfit's torso. During Time Cell Moon Palace, the user will stay in their Awakening Outfit until the domain breaks. *[[Characters#Base Only|Base-only characters]] (including {{Strongest Of History}}) will not switch to the player's Awakening Outfit when using their Awakening moves, except for: **{{Aspiring Mangaka}}, applying the outfit during Foresight's cutscene. **{{Black Death}}, applying the outfit to Parthenogenesis' clones. **{{Sky Bender}}, applying the outfit during Temper. *Several emotes also use this gamepass to show off their effects, namely: Carousel, Ex Provocation, Hei Party, Mirror World, and Stand Proud... If the gamepass was not bought, they will default to their current outfit or use the game's mascot: a basic noob avatar with {{Honored One}}'s blindfold. ====Particular Cases==== File:Gojo0.2AwkOutfit.gif|{{Honored One}} (0.2 Domain) File:MahitoAwkOutfit.gif|{{Perfection}} (Super Awakening) File:TodoAwkOutfit.gif|{{Switcher}} (Tzekada) File:NOTMechaAwkOutfit.gif|{{Puppet Master}} (Puppets) File:NaoyaAwkOutfit.gif|{{Head of the Hei}} (Awakening + Domain) File:CharlesAwkOutfit.gif|{{Aspiring Mangaka}} (Foresight) File:KuroAwkOutfits.gif|{{Black Death}} (Clones) File:CrowCharmerAwkOutfits.gif|{{Crow Charmer}} (Spatial Transference) File:UroAwkOutfits.gif|{{Sky Bender}} (Temper)
{{Gamepass |title1=+1 Emote Page |image1= +1 Emote Page.png|Icon |cost={{Robux}} 175 |description=Adds an additional page of emotes}} ====Info==== The '''+1 Emote Page''' gamepass adds an additional page to the emote wheel that can be swapped to by pressing the arrows in the middle of the wheel, along with a search bar that allows you to use unequipped emotes without having to enter the inventory. ====Notes==== *This gamepass can be bought multiple times rather than once, and will give a new emote page each time it is bought. *Emote pages work in tandem with the [[Gamepasses#More Emote Slots|More Emote Slots]] gamepass, making all extra pages have 8 slots instead of 4.
{{Gamepass |title1=More Build Saves |image1= Buildicon.png|In-Game |cost={{Robux}} 125 |description=Adds 3 extra save slots for saving your builds in build mode}} ====Info==== The '''More Build Saves''' gamepass grants 3 additional save slots for players to use in [[Build Mode|Free Build]], totalng 6 save slots. Dummy.text:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:'''Dummy'''}} The dummy is a stationary figure positioned outside the cafe, featuring a green square on top of its head that will turn red whenever it is stunned or ragdolled. It will act like a frozen player with 100 HP and 0 ping, and is able to participate in [[Emotes|Partner Emotes]] if one is used near it.
If the dummy is away from its spawn point and hasn't been hit for a full minute, it will run back to the cafe's entrance, unless it is stuck in an enclosed area; if this happens, however, it will be teleported back to the origin. ==List Of Dummies== In the [[Private Servers|Private Server]] settings, the server owner can spawn one of eight dummies (including the original, excluding the Dummy Block) in front of them using commands from the Server section. Additionally, they can also choose to clear all dummies from the map, instantly removing them while respawning the original dummy at its spawn location. {|class="fandom-table" !Name !Description !Picture |- |'''Dummy''' |A regular Dummy without an assigned spawn. | rowspan="3"|[[File:Tze Dummy.png|frameless|center|200x200px]] |- |'''Low HP Dummy''' |Has 1 HP, good to test finishers and [[Gamepasses|custom kill sounds]] on. |- |'''Immortal Dummy''' |Has seemingly infinite HP (about 8999999488) but dies to true one shots ([[Perfection]]'s Idle transfiguration and [[Domain Expansion]]). Good for trying out combos or moves without worrying about the dummy dying. |- |'''Attacking Dummy''' |Always uses {{Vessel}}’s M1s/punches. It can be used to test a few game mechanics such as [[Game Controls|burst]] or counters. |[[File:The Attacking Dummy.png|frameless|center|200x200px]] |- |'''Blocking Dummy''' |Always blocking. A good choice to see if specific moves bypass block or to attempt combos. |[[File:TheBlockingDummyJR.png|center|frameless|200x200px]] |- |'''Bullet Dummy''' |Always using {{Restless Gambler}}’s move, "Reserve Balls". Good for testing bullet counters. |[[File:BulletDummy.png|center|frameless|200x200px]] |- |'''Counter Dummy''' |Always using {{Vessel}}’s counter, "Manji Kick". Perfect for testing whether a move can be countered and for testing combos. |[[File:The counter Dummy.png|frameless|center|200x200px]] |- |'''Evasive Dummy''' |Will attempt to ragdoll cancel or burst whenever it is able to. Its escape bar is visible to the dummy's side, and will always be full when the dummy is spawned. Perfect for combo testing. |[[File:EvasiveDummy.png|center|frameless|200x200px]] |- |'''Dummy Block''' |Spawned using the [[Build Mode#Output Blocks|Dummy Block]]. Can have its health, name, shirt and pants customized, and also has an invinciblity and regeneration scaling toggle. The dummy block will send a signal if the dummy dies. |[[File:Dummy block active.png|center|frameless|200x200px]] |} ==NPCs== NPCs (Non-playable characters) are basically dummies that will target other players and attack them. They are able to dash, jump, and move around. Most importantly, these dummies can use moves on their targets and attack them, but they do not have an Awakening Bar and therefore cannot awaken. {| class="fandom-table" !Name !Description !Picture |- |'''Transfigured Human''' |Spawns when the Transfigured Human item is thrown, and will target the nearest enemy (excludes the user). Gamemodes.text: {{DISPLAYTITLE:'''Gamemodes'''}} Clicking the magnifying glass icon on the top bar opens a menu with six different choices: [[File:gamemodes.png|frameless|right|180px]] [[File:mode.png|frameless|right|180px]] '''Join a Friend''': Allows the player to join one of their friends, provided that their server isn’t full or in a different region. '''Duels''': Compete in 1v1s, 2v2s, and 3v3s+ on randomized maps. '''Custom Servers''': Join private servers hosted by players. '''Roulette''': Engage in fast-paced minigames voted for by players. '''Creator Clash''': Fight with custom movesets uploaded to the workshop. '''Public Servers''': Play in the base game, where the player spawn in upon joining. ==Duels== |-|Duels Menu= When selecting the Duels gamemode, the player will be teleported to a menu where two duel choices are available: Casual and Ranked. [[File:Duel Menu.png|center|450px]] After choosing either, the player must press the "Ready" button at the bottom of the screen to search for a random opponent to face. [[File:TopDuelMenu.png|center|400px]] The top bar lists the following options: *'''Invite to Party''': Opens an invite menu where the player can request to join other parties, or accept/decline incoming requests. **'''Disband Party''': Only available from the party owner when the party has at least 2 members, and allows them to break up the party by removing all other players from it. *'''Region Matchmaking''': Toggles matchmaking within the same region. *'''Return to Main Game''': Sends the player to a public server. [[File:Invite Menu.png|center|450px]] After opening the invite menu, the player will be greeted with 2 tabs. The left tab will display all current parties, their members, and if they are searching for an opponent. Pressing "Request Invite" will send an invite to the party owner which will appear for them on the right tab, with the option to ignore or accept the request. If accepted, the player will join the party. The bottom left of the menu will show all members of the current party, with a crown icon next to its owner. Parties can only host up to 4 players, and a party can only match up against others with the same amount of players. |-|Overall Duels= [[File:Untitled design.jpg|right|225x225px|The fighting arena, preparing for battle.]] After finding an opposing team, players are assigned to the "Sorcerers" or "Curses" team and teleported to the arena: a grassy baseplate with invisible borders on all sides. There are four spawns near the center, two for each team, indicated by color. Players remain immobile as 3-second countdown begins before the match starts. Each team starts with a set of lives (3 for 1v1, 5 for 2v2 and more). To win, deplete the opposing team's lives, or if the timer expires, the team with the most lives remaining wins. Once the match is over, the winner will have their selected [[Victory Flashes|Victory Flash]] play before showing the term: "Shenanigan'd!" in cyan text. Losing triggers the same screen, but in purple text. |-|Casual Duels= ===Binding Vows=== Casual duels also feature a '''''"Binding Vow"''''' mechanic that grants buffs and debuffs. During the period of immobility at the start of the match, three random binding vow options appear on each player's screen. Players can choose one option or wait for the timer to run out to not pick any Binding Vows at all. Here are the six available Binding Vows: {|class="fandom-table" !Name !Effect |- |Revealing One’s Hand |The player gains 110% health, but their move cooldowns, Awakening Bar and ragdoll cancel progress are visible to the enemy. |- |Overtime |90% damage for the players first 2 lives of the match, then 125% for the third. The increased damage is shown by a {{WdsTooltips|toggle = {{{basic-tooltip|''blue cursed energy aura''}}}|content = [[File:Overworked.gif|frameless|200x200px]]}} emanating from the player once they reach their last life. |- |Enchain |The player gains 30% more Awakening. However, once the player awakens, their health will be fully restored but they will be unable to do anything but walk, side dash, and block for 12 seconds. They will also awaken as {{Vessel}}, regardless of their selected character. |- |Taking a Gamble |The player deals 120% damage but they will lose a random move each time they respawn. For some reason as soon as the countdown ends the player will lose a move without respawning. |- |True Love |Gain 30% more Awakening, but the player will awaken immediately once their Awakening Bar is full, and then die once it runs out (exceptions being [[Characters#Base Only|base only characters]]). Additionally, all moves will cost 5% of their Awakening. |- |Never Again |Deal 135% damage, but lose a move after using it twice. |} ===Rematches=== Casual duels are different than Ranked, as the matchmaking isn't guaranteed to provide opponents of similar skill. To make up for this, players are allowed to vote for a rematch twice at the end of the duel. |-|Ranked Duels= [[File:EloLB.png|thumb|'''The Highest Elo leaderboard on the right of the Duels menu.'''|300px|right]] The Ranked experience resembles Casual but excludes the binding vow mechanic. The match begins after a 5-second countdown, and no binding vow options are presented. Instead, the matchmaking itself is altered to enhance the player experience. Ranked features a matchmaking system based on Elo (Estimated Level of Opponent). Players start with 0 Elo points, and gain Elo after each win while losing Elo after every loss. Leaving a match causes a heavy Elo loss, however Elo cannot fall below zero. Additionally, players cannot match with opponents if the Elo gap between them is 50 or higher, and the amount of Elo gained/lost after a match will change depending on the Elo difference between players, ranging from 1 to 10 Elo. ==Custom Servers== [[File:Custom.png|frameless|right|180px]][[File:inf.png|frameless|right|180px]] Custom servers are private servers publicly hosted by their owners. Players can either create their own server or join others to showcase builds, movesets, host tournaments, and more. *How to join a server: *# Choose "Custom Server." *# Refresh the custom server list or enter a server title of your choice (typing a region's abbreviation, such as "EU" for Europe will pull up servers from that region only). *# Press the server you desire to join. [[File:Server.png|frameless|right|180px]] *How to host a server: *# Choose "Custom Server." *# Select "Create A Server." *# Provide a server title and press "Create." You will be teleported to your own server with [[Private Servers|private server commands]], where any player can join. Note that the "Server Name" and "Server Icon" settings will affect how the custom server is displayed for others on the servers list. ==Roulette== |-|Overview= Selecting the Roulette option opens a tab with several server regions to pick from. Players are then taken into a voting lobby where they choose from four minigames by stepping on their pressure plates. Each option shows its current vote count, though voting on a minigame only increases the chance of it being picked rather than guarantee it, and the winning vote will be announced at the top of everyon's screen with a brief description of the minigame. If a player does not wish to participate, they can choose to AFK and wait in the lobby. Any players who lose all their lives in a minigame will be brought back to the lobby as well. Who can either AFK or spectate by being boogie woogied back into the match as a crow, with the ability to fly and scream using your M1. At the end of a minigame, players are brought into a score screen summarizing their performance and rewards through a pointing system, while the [[Victory Flashes|Victory Flash]] of the player with the most points plays before everyone is back to the voting lobby. |-|Minigames= Currently, there are 10 minigames in Roulette, with more to come. {|class="fandom-table" !Minigame !Description !Arena !Icon |- |'''Brain Swap (SWP)''' |Players start with randomized movesets in both base and Awakening, with reduced damage and cooldowns, drawn from the game’s move pool (excluding abilities like Rika, Spike Wrath, Head Splitter.. and all domain expansions). Each death reshuffles movesets, and the goal is to get as many kills as possible. |Large maps |[[File:SWP.jpeg|frameless|center|link=|120x120px]] |- |'''Sorcery Clash (SRC)''' |A team-deathmatch where players are put into two teams, "Sorcerers" and "Curses". Each player has one life and both teams will fight one another until either team loses all of its players or the timer runs out. |Large maps |[[File:SRC.png|frameless|center|link=|120x120px]] |- |'''First to Twelve (FTT)''' |Fight other players with randomized base movesets, increased damage, reduced cooldowns, infinite lives, and no Awakenings, regeneration or burst. Advancing to the next number of kills will give you a different moveset with random base moves. This means that two players with the same number of kills will also have the same moveset consisting of base moves. At 11 kills, the only move is Head Splitter. The first to reach 12 kills wins. |Large maps |[[File:FTT.jpeg|frameless|center|link=|120x120px]] |- |'''Final Showdown (FSD)''' |A juggernaut-esque game mode where one random player is selected to play as {{Strongest Of History}}, whose health scales with the number of active players. These players are put on the "Sorcerers" team are each given 3 lives and the ability to monitor the boss's health and Awakening progress. The boss, however, has only one life. Both the boss and the players cannot regenerate health, and the boss's objective is to drain all of the Sorcerers team's lives, while the players' objective is to team up and kill the boss. The game will end if either of these are accomplished, or the six-minute timer has run out causing the boss to win. |Large maps |[[File:FSD.jpeg|frameless|center|link=|120x120px]] |- |'''End of Journey (EOJ)''' |All players are put into team "Sorcerers" with one life, with waves of [[Items#Transfigured Human|Transfigured Humans]] appearing on each spawn. If a Sorcerer dies, they will spawn as a Transfigured Human with 20 HP, no front dash and infinite lives. Dying again will grant a different moveset, size and color, but they will always use {{Locust Guy}}'s M1s. The Sorcerers have to survive until the timer is over to win, while the Curses have to manage to turn every Sorcerer to their side before the timer ends to win. Parkour is disabled. |Large maps |[[File:EOJ.jpeg|frameless|center|link=|120x120px]] |- |'''Perfection Tag (PFT)''' |One player on the "Perfection" team gets a moveset consisting of a slightly faster Idle Transfiguration move with no cooldown, while all the others on the team "Sorcerers" have their combat disabled, faster running speed, and 1 HP. The defenseless players must run and avoid the common enemy hunting them before the timer ends. Each death will extend the timer by 30 seconds, capping at 3 minutes. |Small maps |[[File:PFT.png|frameless|center|link=|120x120px]] |- |'''American Shenanigans (AMS)''' |All players are put on the same team with friendly fire and one life, and will receive an undroppable gun with infinite ammo. The team is tasked with shooting down crows that spawn throughout the match to earn progress points, though there are various types of crows with special effects: *Jackpot: Has a large HP pool, allowing it to sustain multiple hits. *Transfigured: Spawns multiple curse NPCs. *Overheating beak and feet: Explodes immediately after being hit. *Smoke: Will fly to target the player with the highest score before exploding. Once a player reaches 40 progress points, they will obtain the "God Gun", which is a gun with a significantly increased fire rate that can bypass friendly fire. |Large maps |[[File:kenjaku3024.jpeg|frameless|center|link=|120x120px]] |- |'''Prison Realm (PSR)''' |All players are forced into the domain clash state, overriding their entire movesets and giving them double side dashes along with weaker melee attacks. The prison realm, along with a 15 second timer, will appear over a player's head, giving them faster walkspeed and the ability to transfer the cursed object to whoever they hit. Once the timer is over, the prison realm will seal the last player it tagged, killing them, then swapping to another player. The goal is to be the last one standing. |Small maps |[[File:PSR.png|frameless|center|link=|120x120px]] |- |'''Soul Swap (SSP)''' |Upon spawning, players are offered 3 random movesets with varying rarities (Common, Rare, and Legendary). Movesets will also influence which character the player will be using, depending on its mechanics, while some will be entirely custom-made with the Skill Builder. Each death reshuffles movesets, and the goal is to get as much kills as possible. |Large maps |[[File:SSP.png|frameless|center|link=|120x120px]] |} |-|Rewards= Upon completing a Roulette minigame, players receive rewards based on their performance counted in points, capping at $50. Kills do not count in Roulette, and you will get no reward for them. {|class="fandom-table" !Minigame !Info |- |'''SWP, SRC, FTT, SSP''' | *Each kill gained will grant more points. |- |'''FSD''' | *The amount of damage dealt will decide the amount of points granted to the Sorcerers and the juggernaut. If the player win as the Strongest Of History, they will also receive a special Victory Flash. |- |'''EOJ''' | *For Sorcerers, each kill gained will grant more points. *For Curses, both the amount of kills and the damage dealt will grant more points. |- |'''PFT''' | *The duration spent standing near the tagger will decide the amount of points granted. *The amount of kills gained from tagging players will decide the amount of points granted to the tagger. |- |'''PFC''' | *Each second survived will amount to one point. |- |'''AMS''' | *Each kill gained will grant more points. *Points are also determined by accuracy. |} ==Creator Clash== Creator Clash is a gamemode focused on the [[Build Mode/Workshop|Workshop]], granting access to all players while placing them on a special map to fight with custom characters made by the community itself. However, many limits on visual effects and abilities were implemented in response to broken movesets like the infamous Wonder Of U moveset. ==Public Servers== The standard base game, where players are teleported to a random server with the usual Shinjuku-inspired [[map]] with [[Items|items]] spawning every ten minutes in certain spots. ==Trivia== *SRC used to feature a survival mode for Sorcerers against Curses, and was renamed to EOJ up until {{update|1.39}}. **This was changed to a team deathmatch in {{update|1.41}}, with EOJ readded in {{update|1.50}}. ***In {{update|1.62}}, EOJ was changed again to be a wave-based gamemode. *AMS used to allow players to shoot each other right off the bat, rather than needing to kill an arbitrary amount of NPCs first. This version is generally seen as superior to the current one. *The spectating system in Roulette is a reference to the Black Bird Manipulation technique used by Mei Mei in ''Jujutsu Kaisen''. Note that the crows get swapped into the arena using Boogie Woogie. *Keep in mind that summoning {{Mahoraga}} will take away one of your lives in Ranked or Roulette. *Unlike Roulette’s SRC and FSD, players on the same team can harm each other in Ranked 2v2s. *"Revealing One's Hand" is often considered one of the best binding vows due to its negligible downside, as the cooldown information won't aid the enemy in winning interactions unless they are vigilant for counters/ragdoll cancel in combos. *"Taking a Gamble" is also considered to be a good binding vow as the random move can be cycled each time you respawn or use your Awakening, which allows you to settle for a decent moveset. *"Never Again" used to be considered the worst binding vow, with its damage boost not justifying the trade-off. As of {{update|1.49}}, this became a more justified pick, as moves now have two uses before disappearing instead of one. **Additionally, this binding vow will not account for moves that stay off cooldown, such as successful Supernovas, Eye Catchings or {{Star Rage}}'s cooldown resets. *"True Love" is not recommended for some [[Characters#Base Only|base-only]] characters as well as {{Head of the Hei}}, as it will most likely cause you to waste your Awakening due to it functioning as an attack or counter. However, the player will not die after Awakening if they were using a base only character. *Final Showdown appears to be bugged, as the round tends to end whenever a single player leaves the game, regardless of the team.

Note that the move will only get disabled on ragdoll, but the user is able to toggle the rain off by using it again.

This move grants i-frames upon finishing the spin and is aimable during the windup, but its last tick won't always hit. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 1 Value=104, ~7.42 |Stat 2=COOLDOWN |Stat 2 Value=45s |Image=PlasmaWave.gif}} {{Background|Choso's background.png}} |-|Finishers= {{Ability |Type=MELEE COUNTER |Type Color=blue |No Evasive=y |Name='''Supernova''' |Description=The user punches their target away, while pulling their arm to the point of severing it. The target must have 7 HP or less for this finisher effect to trigger. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 1 Value=Insta-kill |Stat 2=COOLDOWN |Stat 2 Value=None |Image=SupernovaFinisher.gif}} {{Ability |Unblockable=y |Bypasses Ragdoll=y |Interruptible=y |Name='''Blood Edge''' |Description=After the slam, the user raises their arms above their head, preparing to slash and stab the target twelve times before kicking them away. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 1 Value=15 for kick |Stat 2=COOLDOWN |Stat 2 Value=13s |Image=BloodEdgeFinisher.gif}} {{Ability |Type=SPECIAL VARIANT |Type Color=red |Unblockable=y |Bypasses Ragdoll=y |Interruptible=y |Name='''Slicing Exorcism''' |Description=The blood chakram slices through the target's torso, splitting them in half. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 1 Value=Insta-kill |Stat 2=COOLDOWN |Stat 2 Value=13s |Image=SlicingExorcismSpecialFinisher.gif}} ==Pros/Cons== {{ProsCons |pros= *High damage moveset with versatile combos and solid neutral tools. *Supernova orbs easily grant supreme control over neutral, and may force the opponent to be overly passive or aggressive as it is difficult to pay attention to both the user and their bomb. *Effective in parkour if used correctly, because of the great mobility from air Flowing Red Scale: Stack. *Several AoE Awakening attacks to deal with groups of enemies, and single target attacks in case you want to focus on one person. *Wing King is a great way to setup into other attacks, especially when using its orbs to confirm high windup moves like Plasma Wave. *Plasma Wave can be used to punish long windup moves such as domain expansions, while its invincibility frames allow you to shrug off any incoming damage from the original attack. *Immune to Hemorrhage's health drains. |cons= *Convergence is very costly in terms of Awakening, which requires you to deal a substantial amount of damage before being able to reach your usual damage output and combo potential, unless you want to risk missing Supernova's counter which is not a viable strategy. *Several base moves are easily punishable on whiff or windup. *Blood Rain and Plasma Wave are scenario dependent, and you will mostly rely on the other two moves, making its long term damage pretty mediocre. *Lacks a domain expansion, instead having Blood Rain which makes the Awakening period last much shorter. }} ==Combos== |-|Base= {{Combo |sequence1=---- |damage1='''''This character Combos are currently being reworked.
Please don't add any combos whatsoever.''''' |notes1=---- }} |-|Awakening= {{Combo |sequence1=---- |damage1='''''This character Combos are currently being reworked.
Please don't add any combos whatsoever.''''' |notes1=---- }} ==Tips & Techs== ===Tips=== *Aerial Flowing Red Scale's blood orb can be used to propel or catapult you in any desired direction when detonated, and can be used into a charged Piercing Blood for a good combo finisher. **The orb can also launch you a lot farther if you were in a car (either spawned in by the [[Build Mode|Vehicle Block]] or from the [[Emotes|"Jeep"]] emote) or ragdolled (including by the [[Emotes|"Ragdoll"]] emote), due to the car having actual physics. *The variant of Slicing Exorcism works better on multiple players because it redirects to another target after landing on one, while the base move is effective on a single target that you can focus the blood beam on, since dealing its full damage is dependent on your aim and your available Convergence Orbs. **Slicing Exorcism's base variant with 4 orbs also deals enough damage to destroy nearly any domain, including ones with increased HP such as Idle Death Gamble. *To make sure Wing King doesn't get blocked at the end of the attack, you'll need to focus on the player you want to hit before getting to the arm pull part of it, as the last hit will stun them long enough for the pull to land. **Wing King's Convergence orbs allow for many more impressive combos, letting you stall for cooldowns and M1 reset. They can also be used during stun to escape combos. *Plasma Wave can prove to be a decent counter when used during the windup of a domain expansion without invincibility, as the user won't be able to move out of the way shortly after the domain is formed, confirming the attack. **Its also worth using at the end of Awakening as it can refund about half of it. ===Techs=== |-|Beginner= ===={{WdsTooltips |toggle = {{{basic-tooltip|'''Anti-Domain Wave'''}}} |content = [[File:AntidomainWaveZX.gif|frameless|239x239px]]}}==== When caught in a domain expansion during your Awakening, you can punish the caster by using Plasma Wave right in front of them, since they won't be able to evade it due to being held in place by the domain creation. This will not work on Idle Death Gamble, Deadly Sentencing or Authentic Mutual Love, as they provide the user with i-frames for most of the domain's windup. |-|Intermediate= ===={{WdsTooltips |toggle = {{{basic-tooltip|'''Orb Jump'''}}} |content = [[File:OrbJumpZX.gif|frameless|239x239px]]}}==== Using Flowing Red Scale's variant with a blood orb places it down on the floor. Using the special while on or around the blood orb sends you flying in whatever direction you were closer to, allowing you to run from opponents, catch them or to save yourself from falling out of the map. ===={{WdsTooltips |toggle = {{{basic-tooltip|'''Minesweep'''}}} |content = [[File:MinesweepZX.gif|frameless|239x239px]]}}==== Requires the user to have a convergence orb. This tech basically requires you to land an aerial Flowing Red Scale, perform an Edge Extend, turn around to drag the opponent to the mine left behind by Flowing Red Scale, then detonate the mine after Blood Edge's 2nd hit. ===={{WdsTooltips |toggle = {{{basic-tooltip|'''King's Reset'''}}} |content = [[File:KingsResetZX.gif|frameless|239x239px]]}}==== After Wing King is over, any Convergence orbs you hold can be unleashed by pressing your special. A great use is to simply perform 3 M1s, and trigger one to stun the opponent long enough for your M1s to reset. While these orbs do not ragdoll, they will come out of your back before they start homing around you, so you'll need to turn around before triggering an orb in order to extend. Another property of Wing King's orbs is that they can be triggered during stun. So turning to the other side when you're flared into a combo will allow you to escape it, and start you own. ===={{WdsTooltips |toggle = {{{basic-tooltip|'''Fast Charge'''}}} |content = [[File:Blood_Manipulator_Fast_Charge_Tech.gif|frameless|100x65px]]}}==== After doing an uppercut, immediately hold Piercing Blood to confirm a Charged Piercing Blood. However, this technique requires very small ping and some practice. |-|Advanced= ===={{WdsTooltips |toggle = {{{basic-tooltip|'''Charged Piercing Scale'''}}} |content = [[File:ChargedPiercingScaleZX.gif|frameless|239x239px]]}}==== After downslamming an opponent lacking their evasive, landing Aerial Flowing Red Scale on them and immediately holding Piercing Blood while detonating the blood orb on the enemy before they get up (increasing their ragdoll time) is an effective way to confirm a Charged Piercing Blood. ===='''Edge Scale'''==== Right after the animation of Flowing Red Scale is over, there is a small window where you can side dash and grab the enemy with Blood Edge. Though this requires some practice, precision, and good ping to get the hang of it. ==='''Downslam Chaining'''=== Requires Convergence After an uppercut/downslam, you can use aerial Flowing Red Scale:Stack or Supernova to create a blood bomb. Then start m1-ing. When the first m1 ends, detonate the orb, this will ragdoll the opponent long enough for you to downslam them. (Gives lots of evasive) ==Trivia== *During the Awakening animation, red highlights of 3 players (barely visible) will appear behind the user. This is a reference to Choso's brothers in the ''Jujutsu Kaisen'' series, Eso, Yuji, and Kechizu, who manifested in Choso’s mind when he was fighting Kenjaku. *While immune to {{Head of the Hei}}'s high damage from Hemorrhage, the effect will drain the user's Awakening meter. *When {{Blood Manipulator}} blocks an attack, sparks may appear along with a metallic noise. This is possibly a reference to the fact that Choso can harden blood on his skin to use it as armor. **This effect is shared with both {{Cursed Partners}} (when blocking with their katana) and {{Puppet Master}}. *The finisher of Blood Edge might be a reference to Monsoon from Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance, as both characters stab their enemy repeatedly on the floor. *Convergence orbs seem to have some visual bugs as they sometimes don't appear or stay on top of the user's head. If Slicing Exorcism was interrupted, the orbs will remain large. *{{Blood Manipulator}}'s [[Events#April Fools 2026 Event|2026 April Fools]] Name (loving and caring brother) is based off of AniDiscourse's [https://www.youtube.com/shorts/mEEv36N-PK8 "Caring Choso"] short. **These origins are shared with {{Lucky Coward}} (kind scholar), {{Defense Attorney}} (greedy lawyer), {{Switcher}} (menace to society), {{Perfection}} (purifier) and {{Salaryman}} (enjoys beating the life out of). *The art of Unlicensed Rhythm Game's "Pass On" shows {{Blood Manipulator}} taking the place of Gregor from Limbus Company as he talks with {{Star Rage}}. ==Gallery== File:Choso.png|Choso, the inspiration for Blood Manipulator. Community Guidelines.text: {{DISPLAYTITLE:'''Community Guidelines'''}} By joining as a member, you are expected to read and follow certain regulations as soon as possible. Make sure to familiarize yourself with them to avoid any issues. Failure to comply may result in warnings or further consequences, depending on the severity of the violation. ==Rules/Guidelines== '''''The following is a set of discussion rules and editing guidelines that must be followed when accessing the wiki's forum or editing pages on the Jujutsu Shenanigans wiki.''''' |-|Discussion Rules= Discussions are an optional feature provided by fandom that allow users of a wiki to create posts, replies, and interact with other users in general. These guidelines are implemented here to maintain a safe environment for everyone involved: #Remain respectful and keep conversations civil. Do not directly nor indirectly insult, slander, or harass a user under any circumstances. Inflammatory comments intended to spark hostility isn't allowed either. Light-hearted jokes are allowed provided all involved users are comfortable with such comments. If you are asked to stop, please stop. Depending on the severity, you will receive anywhere from a Notice to a Ban. #Block evasion will not be tolerated under any circumstance and will result in a permanent block. If you would like to send a message during a block, or want to discuss the length or validity of your block, contact a staff member on their message wall. #Do not "Necropost". Replying to posts that have remained inactive for at least 2 weeks will result in the post being locked and a warning. #Condense your replies. Do not make three or four replies in a row that convey a point that could've been made in one reply. This also applies to posts made with the sole intention of inflating your post count or the amount of replies on a post. If violated, you will receive a notice. #Posts addressing sensitive topics should be avoided. These include suicide/self-harm, politics, personal information, etc. Your post/reply will be deleted and you will receive a notice. #Posts/replies containing offensive content are strictly prohibited and will be deleted immediately. Such topics include suggestive content, racism, bigotry, gore, etc. If you are unsure if a post breaks this guideline, notify a staff before posting it, or just don't post it at all. Slight euphemisms are allowed provided everyone involved is comfortable. Depending on the severity, you will be either warned or banned. #Posts in a language other than English will be deleted and met with a Notice. This is due to foreign comments being difficult to moderate by a primarily English speaking Staff Force. If you can't speak proper English, you can use a translator. #Properly categorize your posts. This allows users to properly filter and sort through posts of a certain desired topic. If you are unsure what category to post in, refer to the categorization guide below. Repeated violations will result in a Notice. #Please keep all replies to a post relevant and on-topic. Continuously Derailing a conversation will be met with a Notice from staff, and will get the post locked. #No NSFW or any sort of suggestive language. This is a wiki for a roblox game, a platform consisting mostly of children. ===Categorization=== *General - This category should be used for any post that doesn't fit in any of the other categories but is still related to Jujutsu Shenanigans. *Memes - This category should be used for any humorous posts or media about Jujutsu Shenanigans. *Unrelated - This category should be used for any post that isn't related to Jujutsu Shenanigans in any way. Takes priority over other categories. For example, if you post a poll about another game, it should be in the Unrelated category instead of the Polls and Questions category. *Polls and Questions - Should be used for posts that are of the Poll type. *Suggestions/Concepts - This category should be used for any text-based suggestions or concepts for the development Jujutsu Shenanigans. Should not be confused for the "Creation Showcase" category. An example would be a conceptual moveset for a new character. *Creation Showcase - Any visual fan-made content should be put in this category. An example would be fanart of Jujutsu Shenanigans. *Wiki/Staff Related - This category should only be used for posts with the purpose of improving the wiki or the staff team. An example would be a template concept. *Major Announcements - Should not be used by ANYONE other than staff members! This will only be used for major wiki announcements, like staff applications. |-|Staff Guidelines= If a staff member violates any of these guidelines, please report it to an [[Wiki Staff#Bureaucrats and Administrators|Admin or above]]. #Staff will follow all the discussions guidelines mentioned earlier above. #Staff will deliver punishments in an impartial, fair manner with reference from the official discussions guidelines above. This includes post locks/unlocks and post/reply deletions. If a user believes a decision taken was unfair, an appeal should be made. #Staff will maintain a respectful, formal tone when delivering punishments. |-|Editing Guidelines= '''For more information on editing the ''Jujutsu Shenanigans Wiki'', see the wiki's [[Manual of Style]].''' *Always keep information up to date. As new updates are released, new content should be added to maintain the wiki's accuracy. You can use the [[Manual of Style]] to ensure your edits follow the wiki's standard format. *Make sure all edits are related to '''"Jujutsu Shenanigans"''' and avoid adding content that is unrelated to the game. *Always check your edits for spelling and grammatical errors. *Each character page should include categories at the top to help users navigate the wiki and easily find what they’re looking for. *Never include personal or public opinions when editing a page. Information should remain factual and unbiased. *Avoid repeatedly reverting edits without providing an explanation. Instead, explain what is wrong with the edit using the appropriate discussion space or point it out in the comment section below. *Ensure that all images used on a page are relevant to the article and the content being discussed. *Create your own GIFs instead of using GIFs made by other people. '''''If you think anything should be changed or added, don't hesitate to contact staff through the [[Wiki Staff]] page to find someone who can help with page protection, edits, and more.''''' ==Punishment System== Staff members can issue any of three different punishments: (If you believe a punishment to be unfair, appeal to a [[Wiki Staff#Bureaucrats and Administrators|High Ranking Staff]] by leaving a message on your own wall.) NOTICES: A notice is an undocumented warning given to you typically for very minor offenses. An example may be repeatedly miscategorizing a post. If a staff member has given you multiple notices for a minor offense, they may be more inclined to give you a warning next time. WARNINGS: A warning is a documented warning given for moderate offenses. They will be documented under a locked "Warnings" sub-page on your profile. These can be appealed by Thread moderators and above. An example is repeatedly insulting a user after several requests to stop. BLOCKS: A block is a site-wide restriction from any social activity for heavy offenses. An example is posting highly inappropriate content or doxxing a user. These can be appealed by an Administrator or above. If a user has been banned twice, the third time is likely to be permanent.
