Build Mode.text:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:'''Build Mode'''}} {{BuildTabs}} [[File:Builder.png|center|frameless|400x400px]] '''Build Mode''' (also simply called building) is a feature added in {{Update|1.15}} that allows you to build structures and logic-based creations, and can only be accessed in a [[Private Servers|Private Server]]. To enable Build Mode, press "M" or enable "Free Build" using Private Server commands on the "Players" section. While Free Build is active, the selected player can use their moveset, M1, dash or block. However, they have constant total i-frames. ==Build Shortcuts== *Pressing '''M''' will toggle '''Build Mode'''. *Pressing '''N''' will toggle '''Flight'''. *You can '''cut, copy and paste''' objects with '''Ctrl + X, Ctrl + C and Ctrl + V''', which can also be done between saves if you load a save, then paste an object copied from a previous save. *Pressing '''Ctrl + Z''' will '''undo''' your last action. *'''Holding Ctrl''' while selecting an object will not deselect the previously selected object, allowing you to '''multi-select''' blocks. *Pressing '''T''' will cycle between selection tools (Position, Rotation, and Size). *Pressing '''Y''' will cycle between local axis and global axis. ==Building Blocks== There are currently '''7''' building blocks that can be spawned: [[File:BuildBlocks.png|frameless|right]] *'''Part''': Spawns a default block. *'''Spawnpoint''': Spawns a player spawnpoint. Giving this object a color assigns it to a team with that specific color. *'''Trusses''': Spawns in a default cubic truss/ladder. *'''Image''': Spawns a black square with the game's default icon on one of its sides. When selected, you can change the Image/Decal ID to your preference, alongside being able to toggle its dark background. * '''Wedge''': Spawns a default ramp. *'''Texture''': Spawns a black square with the game's default icon on one of its sides, and will repeatedly display it depending on that surface's dimensions. When selected, you can change the Image/Decal ID, its width and its length (both defaulted to 1) to your preference, alongside being able to toggle its dark background. *'''Mesh''': Spawns a default block, this block will only look different if a [https://create.roblox.com/store/meshparts Mesh ID] is provided. In order to give this block a texture, the Texture ID will need to be filled in as well; Giving this object a color will just change the color of the mesh, but the texture will override the color. In order to modify the size of the mesh, the scale must be filled in. ===Selection Menu=== When a building block (other than Images and Textures) is selected, a secondary menu made of 2 parts will pop up: ====Primary Menu==== [[File:Selection1.png|frameless|right]] *'''Can Collide''': Toggles the collision of the selected building block. *'''Cast Shadow''': Toggles shadows casting from the selected building block. *'''Breakable''': Toggles the destructibility of the selected building block. Wedges and Trusses are unaffected by this, and will remain unbreakable. *'''Neutral''': Only available for spawnpoints. Turning it off disables it for the default "Neutral" player team, limiting the spawn to other teams only. *'''Delete Part''': Deletes the selected object. Appears when Logic Blocks are selected as well. ====Secondary Menu==== [[File:Selection2.png|frameless|right]] *'''R, G, B''': Allows you to customize the color of the selected building block using rgb color values (red, green, blue). *'''Transparency''': Scales the transparency of the selected building block to values with 0 being opaque and 1 being invisible (Although you can go between and beyond that). *'''Materials''': Changes how the skin of selected building block looks. Current materials are: Plastic, Smooth Plastic, Glass, Metal, Brick, Slate, Grass, Wood, Wood Planks, Neon, Forcefield, Concrete, Sand, Diamond Plate, Granite, Fabric, Marble, Foil. (Add new materials here please) *'''Color Picker''': Allows you to customize the color of the selected building block, while also being able to alter its shade using the slider on the right. ==Logic Blocks== Logic Blocks are parts that can provide additional functionality to [[Private Servers]] through advanced means, and were added in {{update|1.32}}, allowing for more innovative builds. These blocks are invisible out of Free Build, and function using an ID system, where blocks send and receive signals from other blocks with the same ID. Logic Blocks are split into 4 types: Input, Output, Interaction and Logic Gates. |-|Input Blocks= Input Blocks will send an output signal to other blocks when they activate, yet only if a certain condition is fulfilled. Currently, there are only '''4''' Input Blocks in Build Mode: {|class="wikitable" !style="background: #FFEE55;" |'''Block''' !style="background: #FFEE55;" |'''Description''' |- |
'''Touch'''
| *Once the HumanoidRootPart (torso) of a player (out of Free Build and don't possess i-frames) fully steps in it, the block will activate. |- |
'''Prompt'''
| *Will activate once '''"E"''' is pressed/held (clicking on the pop-up works as well). **You can choose the name of the prompt, and how long it should be held for. |- |
'''Voice Relay'''
| *Functions as a microphone, outputting any audio emitted by players inside of it through a speaker part. **To place the "speaker" part, select the block and press '''Set Output Destination'''. You can then select the output destination and move it anywhere you wish. **''Unlike the other input blocks, this block does not send an output signal; its sole purpose is to stream voice chat over a distance.'' |- |
'''Connect'''
| *Will turn on once an ability with the right [[Build Mode/Skill Builder|Connect node]] signal has been used. **A Connect's signal works similarly to a block's ID: Any Connect block with the same signal as a Connect node will turn on once that node is reached on the custom ability's timeline when that ability is used. **Range will determine how close the user of the ability needs to be to the Connect block for it to pick up the signal. **The duration of the signal is customized on the Connect node. |} |-|Output Blocks= Once an Output Block gets an output signal from an Input Block, it will activate and perform a unique command. Currently, there are only '''6''' Output Blocks in Build Mode: {|class="wikitable" !style="background: #FF4E4E;" |'''Block''' !style="background: #FF4E4E;" |'''Description''' !style="background: #FF4E4E;" |'''Extra Functionality''' |- |
'''Sound Block'''
| *Plays an audio when on. The sound can be picked by typing in its ID, obtained from the Roblox Marketplace, and you can choose its volume and how far (in studs) it can be heard from. | *'''"Loop"''' will make the sound restart once it's over infinitely, but as long as it's getting an output signal. |- |
'''Vehicle Block'''
| *Spawns a jeep when activated. Only one can spawn from the block at a time. Jump inside the jeep to pilot it. | *None. |- |
'''Team Block'''
| *Creates a team. You are able to name the team, and choose the color of its icon and name on the leaderboard. Same colored spawnpoints with the "Neutral" option toggled off will be assigned to a team. (Setting the colour of the team to pure white causes bugs with the leaderboard) | *Like Interaction Blocks, the Team Block will assign a player to a team if their HumanoidRootPart (torso) is inside of it while it's getting a signal. |- |
'''Mover Block'''
| *Functions as an indestructible building part that will move to a selected destination when it gets a signal. This block is made up of 2 parts: **Origin Part: The main part of the block. "Select Destination" will select the other part of the mover block. "Reset Destination" will move the destination and overlap it with the origin. You can choose the duration that the origin will take to travel to the destination. This part is visible outside of Build Mode, and pulls up the secondary building block selection menu. **Destination Part: Spawns in the middle of the sky after "Select Destination" is used for the first time. "Select Origin" will select the main part of the block. "Reset Destination" remains the same. This part is invisible outside of Build Mode, and cannot have its size altered. | *None |- |
'''Dummy Block'''
| *Spawns a special dummy when it gets a signal. You can customize the dummy's name, HP, along with clothing (only shirt and pants) using IDs from the Roblox Marketplace. | *'''"Invincible"''' will make the dummy invulnerable. *'''"Regen Scaling"''' will make the dummy's regeneration scale with their customized HP, from 1 HP per second when off to 1% HP per second when on. *If the dummy dies, the block will send a signal to whatever is connected to it. |- |
'''NPC Block'''
| *Spawns a special NPC when it gets a signal. It will automatically attack players on sight, but you can customize its name, HP, along with clothing (only shirt and pants) using IDs from the Roblox Marketplace. | *The NPC's '''"Playstyle"''' can also be chosen, with the block offering 4 different playstyles: **'''''Aggressive''''': Will ruthlessly follow its target, dashing around them and performing 3 to 4 M1s before using a move if it has any. **'''''Passive''''': Will approach the target in a less aggressive manner, blocking and refraining from front dashing. **'''''Masher''''': Will simulate mashing a keyboard, using any move it has anytime it could. **'''''Bandit''''': Will aggressively pursue the target, only without dashing or blocking. *'''"Target NPCs"''' will allow the NPC to only target NPCs when on, and will not target players. *'''"Regen Scaling"''' will make the NPC's regeneration scale with their customized HP, from 1 HP per second when off to 1% HP per second when on. *If the NPC dies, the block will send a signal to whatever is connected to it. |} |-|Interaction Blocks= Interaction Blocks are similar to Output Blocks, but in order to apply their effects, the hurtbox of a player who possesses no i-frames whatsoever (including Free Build's) must be inside the Interaction Block while they're getting an output signal, meaning they must be powered and scaled to fit players inside. In the case of powering an Interaction Block with a Touch Block, it is best to overlap both blocks. {|class="wikitable" !style="background: #77FF44;" |'''Block''' !style="background: #77FF44;" |'''Description''' !style="background: #77FF44;" |'''Extra Functionality''' |- |
'''Damage Block'''
| *Deals damage each second. You can change how much damage is inflicted every tick or use negative damage to heal instead. | *Enabling '''"Max HP"''' will change the block's use from harming players to defining a maximum health cap value. ''(e.g: giving oneself 300 Max HP as {{Perfection}} will set the health-bar to 100/300, instead of 300/300.)'' |- |
'''Boost Block'''
| *Launches you in a designated direction using vectors (x, y, z). | *None. |- |
'''Moveset Block'''
| *Grants a chosen move. You can customize the move's cooldown, tooltip and assign a move slot to occupy, and the move can be picked from a list to the right of the menu (includes a few replaced moves). | *Clicking "Custom" on the moves list will pull up the {{Skill Builder}} in order to create a custom move. *Enabling '''"Add"''' automatically adds the move to the empty slot with the smallest number (1–8) instead of assigning it to a specific chosen slot. *Typing anything in '''"Display Name"''' will cause the original move's name to be replaced with the text inserted when the move gets added to a moveset. |- |
'''Erase Block'''
| *Fully erases the player's moveset. | *None. |- |
'''Teleport Block'''
| *Teleports you to a specified location. You can customize the destination by selecting the block, moving to the place you want to be teleported to, and then pressing '''"Set Destination"'''. | *'''"Select Destination"''' allows you to select the destination part of the Camera Block, while '''"Reset Destination"''' will overlap it with the origin. |- |
'''Scale Block'''
| *Changes the player's model to a chosen size. | *None. |- |
'''Item Block'''
| *Grants a chosen [[Interactables|item]] when it gets a signal. You can choose how long the item stays before despawning. | *'''"Disable Drop"''' will allow you to keep hold of the item, even if you were hit or ragdolled *'''"Disable Durability"''' will give the item infinite usage. |- |
'''Fun Block'''
| *Toggles off the selected [[Settings|fun setting]]. | *'''"Set"''' will reverse the block's behavior, making it turn on the selected [[Settings|fun setting]] instead. |- |
'''Camera Block'''
| *Sets the camera to a selected destination. Unlike other blocks, '''"Set Destination"''' will set the destination part to your camera's position, and not your character's. | *'''"Select Destination"''' allows you to select the destination part of the Teleport Block, while '''"Reset Destination"''' will overlap it with the origin. |- |
'''Speed Block'''
| *Changes the player's walkspeed. | *Negative values will not allow the player to move, while an infinite value will break their character. |- |
'''Special Block'''
| *Replaces the player's character special with another custom-made special. You're only able to customize its cooldown, but not the bar's color. | *Clicking "Custom" will pull up the {{Skill Builder}} in order to create a custom special. |- |
'''Awakening Block'''
| *Replaces the player's awakening with a custom-made one. You're only able to customize its name and duration, but not the bar's color. | *Clicking "Custom" will pull up the {{Skill Builder}} in order to create a custom awakening sequence. |- |
'''Accessory Block'''
| *Grants an accessory when on. The accessory can be picked by typing in its ID, obtained from the Roblox Marketplace. | *None. |- |
'''Character Block'''
| *Changes the player's selected character to a custom-made one. You're able to base the custom-made character on a pre-existing one, pick the character's name, and adorn it with an icon. | *Clicking "Configure" will pull up a menu with 5 attributes that will make up the character: Skill, Special, Awakening, Melee, and Chase. These attributes can be customized using the edit option, which will pull {{Skill Builder}}. Additionally, other settings must be used to optimise these attributes: **For Skills, you are able to customize the skill's cooldown, tooltip and the assigned move slot. Enabling '''"Add"''' will override the selected slot and randomize which keys (1-8) the moves are bound to. **For Specials, you are able to customize the special's cooldown. **For Awakenings, you are able to customize the Awakening's duration and how long it will take for the [[Awakening Outfits|Awakening Outfit]] gamepass to activate. **For Chase (front dash), you are able to customize the chase's cooldown. ***Names can be given to all attributes, though they will only be visible on skills and awakenings when using the character. **Additionally, you can import/export a character's configuration by using the clipboard icons at the bottom of the "Configure" menu, allowing you to share and receive custom characters made by other players. *"Show In List" will allow the character to be selected from the in-game character list, where its name is shown in blue next to its icon. |- |} |-|Logic Gates= Rather than sending a signal after a simple condition, Logic Gates change how given signals are sent/recieved, and can effectively alter how Input blocks interact with Output/Interaction blocks. There are currently '''5''' Logic Gates: {|class="wikitable" !style="background: #55FFFF;" |'''Block''' !style="background: #55FFFF;" |'''Description''' |- |
'''AND Gate'''
| *Will send a signal once it gets every output signal from a certain amount of connected blocks. **''"Threshold"'' determines how many blocks are needed to turn on the AND Gate, and is defaulted to 1 (ex: If 3 Input Blocks share its ID while it has a threshold of 3, the AND Gate will send an output signal once all 3 Input Blocks are on). |- |
'''Light Block'''
| *Emits faint light when on. This block can also function as an Input Block if you add in the same Output ID of your chosen block while the Light Block is getting a signal. **'''"Flip"''' will make whatever Input Block connected to it function similarly to a switch, requiring a signal everytime you wish to turn the Light Block on or off. **''This block is visible even if Build Mode is off.'' |- |
'''NOT Gate'''
| *Reverses the output signal of blocks with the same Input/Output ID. (ex: If an Input Block is on while connected to the NOT Gate, the Output/Interaction Block connected to it will be off, and vice versa.) |- |
'''Timer Block'''
| *Sends a given output signal after a certain delay in seconds. |- |
'''XOR Gate'''
| *Will activate whenever it receives an amount of output signals equal to its threshold, or none. **''"Threshold"'' determines how many blocks are needed to turn off the XOR Gate, and is defaulted to 1 (ex: If 3 Input Blocks share its ID while it has a threshold of 3, the XOR Gate will stop working whenever none or all of the Input Blocks turn on). |} ==Build Tools== [[File:Menu1.png|frameless|right|150x150px]][[File:Menu2.png|frameless|right|150x150px]][[File:Menu3.png|frameless|right|150x150px]] *'''Move Value''': Changes the step of the Position and Size Tools. This is set to 1 stud by default. *'''Rotate Value''': Changes the step of the Rotation Tool. This is set to 45° by default. *'''Selection Tools''': Pressing this or '''T''' will cycle between 3 tools: **''Position'': Allows you to move an object by dragging the purple arrows. This is the default tool. **''Rotation'': Allows you to rotate an object by dragging red, yellow, and blue dots. **''Size'': Allows you to change the size of an object by dragging the purple dots. *'''Undo''': Reverts your last action. *'''Clone''': Makes a duplicate of the selected block, while also copying its info: Color, Size, ID, etc. *'''Logic Wires''': Toggles the visibility of colored lines that appear when 2 Logic Blocks are connected (Input to Output). *'''Axis''': Toggles the multiselection between having a Local Axis (relative to the part's orientation) or Global Axis (relative to the world's orientation). *'''Remove All Spawns''': Removes all spawnpoints placed on the main [[map]], except the ones you have placed. *'''Saves''': Takes you to a tab allowing you to interact with your 3 save slots (6 with the [[More Build Saves]] [[Gamepasses|gamepass]]). These save slots can be renamed, and each slot can hold up a little over 4.3 MB of memory. Each of the save slots has the 2 following commands: **'''Load''': Removes every placed part/block from the map and loads a build from the selected slot instead. **'''Load Version''': Moves to another tab to load a build from a list of all the saves done on the selected slot within the last 30 days. **'''Save''': Saves every placed part/block on a selected slot. **'''Autosave''': This slot saves the last build on your private server before you leave, which is why the only command is loading what's on it as you can't manually save any progress on the autosave except by leaving the server. Though it may be risky as it might not save all your progress, so it's best used for recovering progress when everyone is kicked from the server due to an update, connection loss, etc.. *'''Clear All Parts''': Removes all the parts you have placed. Once clicked, a prompt will pop up, asking if you're sure you want to delete all the blocks placed (even if you didn't place any) before they get cleared. ==Build Tips== *In some cases, using a single NOT Gate is much better than multiple Input Blocks, as the NOT Gate doesn't need any scaling, overlaying or activation and won't cause as much lag as multiple Input Blocks. **The best example is using a singular NOT gate to turn every connected block into effectively a "Touch Block", toggling them on when you walk into them. This, again, saves up on a majority of lag. *Moveset Blocks may not have new moves on their list, but typing in the name of the move will still grant it to you. **This is also true for Item Blocks, as the [[Items#Broom|Broom]] item is not in the block's item list, but can be obtained by typing it in. *Moveset and Teleport Blocks have a delay before interacting with the player. After saving the build and loading it, the delay disappears for Teleport Blocks. This makes it tricky to make custom movesets due to the Teleport Block transporting players before the Moveset Block grants them a move, but it can be fixed by adding a Timer Block to delay the activation of the Teleport Block. *Deleting the main map is impossible due to it being made of indestructible parts and going back to normal after you leave and rejoin your server (even with "Destruction Respawns" turned off). To deal with this, make a build somewhere else away from the main map (above or to the side), and place your own spawns on it, then delete the main map's spawns. You can also set up a large teleport block over the main map to instantly send players straight to your build, but you can only have one spawn point if you do that. (Mainly used for lobbies and Workshop maps) *At times, Team Blocks reset your selected team color for apparently no reason. The issue is that teams on Roblox Leaderboards only allow colors from the [https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/datatypes/BrickColor BrickColor] datatype, and any other color that isn't on that list will be rounded to the closest color. **Moreover, Team Blocks cannot occupy the same color, and will randomize the RGB inputted to avoid having the same color as other teams. **The Neutral team's color is white (RGB: 255, 255, 255). ===Notable Issues=== *When trying to scale a block with the "Size" tool, there is a chance that the purple circles will not move upon being dragged or become inverted. This can be easily fixed by saving the build and reloading it. *Setting the step value for the Position and Size tools to 0 may be ideal for smoother builds, but be aware that this will cause any spawned blocks to appear in the void. On top of that, setting it to a value lower than the selected part's Y size will make it impossible to resize other axes. *Selecting two Character Blocks and clicking Configure will combine the two and potentially delete moves. Due to this it is heavily recommended to place multiple Character Blocks far away from each other. *When doing '''Ctrl + Z''' it will undo the last action throughout the SERVER, not just you, so be careful when undoing. ===Logic Builds=== This section is dedicated to advanced logic setup that fulfill certain mechanics that are otherwise not in the game. Note that: *None of the given IDs are mandatory as long as the blocks have the corresponding circuit connection. *Preferably use Prompt Blocks as Input. *The Threshold on all AND Gates is 2. *'''''None''''' signifies leaving the ID space empty, while '''''Anything''''' signifies an ID for any block you wish to connect the circuit to. |-|Timed Signal= *'''Timed Signal''': Will send a timed signal that lasts for a certain amount of time, chosen by picking the Timer Block's delay. **Setup:

You can pick any Input Block of your choice, and choose how long the loop takes before switching off then back on by picking the Timer Block's delay. **Notes: ***Not much different than an automatic repeater, as the only notable difference is needing to be triggered by an Input Block. **Setup:

Will need an Input Block as a primer. **Notes: ***All Timer Blocks delays should stay at 0.1 or 0.2 seconds. ***By using a Light Block from the chain to turn on an Output or Interaction Block, that block will essentially get powered randomly after a certain duration. Using each Light Block for an Output or Interaction block will make a randomizer, turning one block at a time. ***After a while, the repeater will stop functioning properly due to issues like ping, as multiple Timer and Light Blocks get powered at once. **Setup:

You can pick any Input Block of your choice, and choose how long the cooldown is by picking the Timer Block's delay. **Notes: Light Block 5 will indicate that the cooldown is over if it's off. **Setup:
{|class="wikitable" style="text-align:center" !style="background: white;" |'''Block''' !style="background: white;" |'''Input ID''' !style="background: white;" |'''Output ID''' |- |'''AND Gate''' |cdLight1 |cdAND |- |'''NOT Gate''' |cdLight2 |cdNOT |- |'''Timer Block''' |cdAND |cdTimer |- |'''Input Block''' |'''''None''''' |cdInput |- |'''Light Block 1''' |cdInput |cdLight1 |- |'''Light Block 2''' |cdNOT |cdLight1 |- |'''Light Block 3''' |cdAND |'''''Anything''''' |- |'''Light Block 4''' |cdAND |cdTimer |- |'''Light Block 5''' |cdTimer |cdLight2 |}
|-|Randomizer= *'''Randomizer''': You know what this does. **Notes: ***All Timer Block delays should stay at 0.1 seconds. ***This is basically a repeater, but with 3 other parts focused on keeping it functional in order to get one and only one result out of the Light Blocks: ****'''Trigger''': Turns the repeater on and makes sure it never stops working. ****'''Selector''': Picks up all the Light Block signals from the repeater chain that are currently on, and sends them towards the Limiter. ****'''Limiter''': Singles out one signal by deactivating the others, allowing it to reach its corresponding final Light Block. ***''If you want more than four randomized results, just continue the existing pattern by adding new Logic Blocks in sequence while making sure to keep the same input and output logic so the randomizer cycles through all blocks evenly.'' ****For example, if you wish to have a 1 in 5 chance, you need a Light Repeat9, Timer Repeat10, AND Gate 5, Light Comp5, Light EXPO5, NOT Gate 5, NOT Gate E, Light A4, B4, C4, D4, E1, E2, E3, E4, and a 5th final Light. **Setup:

[[Category:Characters]][[Category:Complete_Characters]] {{DISPLAYTITLE:'''Defense Attorney'''}} {{Character2 |title1={{Defense Attorney}} |image1= YHigurumaBase.jpg|Base YHigurumaUlt.jpg|Domain Awakening YHigurumaUlt2.jpg|True Awakening |cost=Free |hp=90 |special= *'''No Escape''' *'''Domain Amplification''' |previous={{Switcher}} |next={{Cursed Partners}} |domain_awakening='''Deadly Sentencing''' |true_awakening='''Death Penalty''' }} {{Quote|If everyone told the truth, we wouldn't need trials.|Hiromi Higuruma ({{Defense Attorney}}) to Yuji Itadori ({{Vessel}})}} ==Description== Defense Attorney is the 6th [[Characters#Early Access|Early Access]] and 10th [[Characters|character]] added to ''Jujutsu Shenanigans.'' ===Origin=== {{Origin |Defense Attorney is based off of Hiromi Higuruma, a character from ''Jujutsu Kaisen''. |{{JJK|Hiromi Higuruma}} is an antagonist turned ally who, before becoming a sorcerer and a Culling Game competitor, used to be a very experienced lawyer and preferred taking difficult cases to help the wrongfully judged. ==Pros & Cons== {{ProsCons |pros= *Versatile base moveset with moderate cooldowns and satisfactory mobility. *Benefits from interruptions and excels at countering passive plays. *Deadly Sentencing is the safest domain in the game, as its invulnerability can be used as a defensive measure, and you can then attempt to confiscate the enemy's remaining attacks all while getting healed and/or Awakening. *Longer M1 range in Awakening, along with the potential to easily one shot opponents due to Execution stacks being shared by most moves. *Domain Amplification can allow the user to avoid high-damage projectiles and lets them be more aggressive, as they're guaranteed to stay unpunished. |cons= *Punishable endlag on miss/block for several base moves. *Lower max HP. *Failing a mix up yields barely any damage and immediately reset to neutral by ending combos. *Loses out on damage due to M1 count changing after a block break or regular move. *The entire domain can be denied after 6 wrong guesses, and most Awakening moves lack i-frames and/or instead have long windups and high endlag. *Domain Amplification is prioritised over block, and cannot prevent all damage/stun from multi-hit attacks (such as Plasma Wave, Rabbit Escape, Dismantle..). }} ==Combos== |-|Base= {{Combo |sequence1=---- |damage1='''''This character Combos are currently being reworked.

This does not apply during other results as you'll be stunned from the Executioner Sword's Awakening sequence. *Deadly Sentencing's Confiscation will often target "moveset switching" abilities to indirectly take away more than one move from enemies. These abilities being {{Ten Shadows}}' Switch, {{Cursed Partners}}' Rika, and {{Lucky Coward}}'s Helping Hand. **In {{Hired Hunter}}'s case, the domain will confiscate their equipped weapon instead of the special. *Winning a domain clash automatically fills one segment of the Judgement Bar inside Deadly Sentencing. *Domain Amplification will protect the user from all attacks, which includes moves such as Unrestricted Density. **Note that while Embodiment Of Self Perfection's transfiguration is nullified, the bar drain is not. If their transfiguration bar was empty, the user will die once Domain Amplification is dispelled. *While awakened, {{Restless Gambler}} will regenerate limbs whenever using Rhythm. Build Mode/Skill Builder.text:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:'''Skill Builder'''}}{{Outdated}}{{BuildTabs}} The '''Skill Builder''' is a feature added to Free Build in {{update|1.57}}, which allows players to create their own custom abilities as an extension to the Moveset, Awakening, Special, and Character Blocks, using pre-existing abilities, visuals and animations. It was given a major overhaul in {{update|1.60}} to include specials and many more features. To access the Skill Builder, place down a Moveset, Awakening, or Special Block using [[Build Mode]] and select "Custom" in the block's list of abilities, or alternatively place a Character Block and access the "Configure" menu then "Edit" a character's skills, awakening, specials, M1s (melee), or front dashes (chase). This will pull up the Skill Builder menu which consists of the 3 main tabs: #'''''Timeline''''': Where the custom move is structured. #'''''Conditions''''': Where the custom move is limited in usage on selected factors. #'''''Properties''''': Where miscellaneous tweaks are edited. Be aware that the ability's name, cooldown, and key bind have to be customized from the block's menu itself. |-|Timeline= The Timeline is the main tab for skill building, and includes a list of nodes that will comprise the custom move. Pressing a node will place it on the timeline and select it, causing its menu to replace the node list. While selected, you're able to remove the selected node using "-", copy it, paste it, move it up and down in the timeline ("^" and "⌄"), or deselect it by pressing it again. If no node is selected, all the buttons will default to the branch, but it cannot be deleted if it's the Default one. The custom move will only account for nodes under the 150 second limit unless the branch is with recent activity and has the "no cancel" property on. {|class="fandom-table" !Block !Information |- |'''
Wait
''' | *Allows the user to set a gap between nodes wherever this node is placed on the timeline, using the setting '''''Time''''' which will stall the activation of the next node on the timeline for the chosen duration (defaulted to 1 second). |- |
'''Sound'''
| *Adds a custom sound effect by inputting a working ID from the [https://create.roblox.com/store/audios|Roblox Creator Store], which will play when the custom move reaches this node on the timeline all while according to the following settings: **'''''Volume''''': Determines how loud the sound effect will be, set to 0.5 by default. **'''''Speed''''': Determines the speed of the audio, set to 1 by default. **'''''Start''''': Determines the start of the sound effect, cutting off anything before, set to 0 by default. **'''''End''''': Determines the end of the sound effect, cutting off anything after, set to 500 by default. **'''''Fade In''''': Determines the amount of time needed to transition to the desired volume from the starting point, set to 0 by default. **'''''Fade Out''''': Determines the amount of time needed to transition from the desired volume to mute from the ending point, set to 0 by default. **'''''Cancel''''': When on, the node will instead cancel any Sound node currently playing the same audio ID. **'''''Global''''': Allows the sound to play for all players anywhere. **'''''Projectile Tag''''': Attaches the sound to a projectile with the same Projectile Tag. |- |
'''Velocity'''
| *Grants control over the user's movement when activating the custom move. Several settings accompany this node: **'''''Force''''': Determines the distance and direction that the user will be traveling to using coordinates on the XYZ axis, where X is horizontal (right to left), Y is vertical (down to up), and Z is depth (backwards to forwards), all in studs and defaulted to 0. **'''''Time''''': Determines how long the user will move in said direction, in seconds. **'''''Fade''''': When off, the user will only halt with sudden stops. When on, the user's velocity will decrease until it reaches 0. **'''''Track''''': Determines whether the user's velocity adjusts to where they're facing at all times instead of where they last faced before the node is reached on the timeline. **'''''Relative From Branch''''': Determines if the target's velocity stay relative to the user rather than themselves if applied through a "Branch Target" setting from another node. **'''''Last Hit''''': Normally set to -1, stands for how long the user can apply the same velocity to the target they last attacked. **'''''Ragdoll''''': Applies ragdoll for a chosen duration, setting this value to -1 will cancel ragdoll. **'''''True Ragdoll''''': Makes the '''''Ragdoll''''' setting disable ragdoll cancel. Note that true ragdoll does not pause ragdoll duration when mid-air. |- |
'''Connect'''
| *Sends an activation signal to a Connect Block once reached on the custom move's timeline: **'''''Signal''''': Basically functions the same as the ID system is for Logic Blocks, syncing the Connect node to any Connect Blocks with the same Signal ID. **'''''Time''''': Determines how long the activation signal lasts for once it reaches a Connect Block. **'''''Range''''': Dictates how close the user must be to the Connect Block in order for the activation signal to be sent from the node to it. |- |
'''Hitbox'''
| *Creates an area where the targets are affected by the user once this keyframe is reached. At the top of the menu, there's a preview featuring a dummy and the hitbox, as well as a preview briefly showing up on the user when changing a value. Many settings come into play to customize this node: **'''''Position''''': Determines the position of the hitbox depending on the user's own position using coordinates on the X Y Z axis, where X is horizontal (left/right), Y is vertical (up/down), and Z is depth (forward/back), all in studs and defaulted to 0, 0, 4. **'''''Size''''': Determines the dimensions of the hitbox, where X is width, Y is height, and Z is depth, all in studs and defaulted to 6. **'''''Rotation''''': Determines the rotation of the hitbox. **'''''Stun''''': Stun targets for the chosen duration in seconds once they're affected by the hitbox. **'''''Stun Anim''''': Forces targets hit by the hitbox to perform the default stun animation when on, off by default. **"""Ignore Wakeup"": Ignores wakeup stun immunity, meaning this still stun the opponent even if they just woke up from ragdoll. This is commonly disabled for custom M1's. **'''''Damage''''': Damages the targets by a chosen amount once they're affected by the hitbox. **'''''Debree''''': Determines the size of the debris created by the hitbox in studs. Having any Debree over 0 will allow it to harm domains, while 0 or below will not create Debree. ***Setting this value to a negative number will instead instantly delete any breakable material instead of leaving debris, with the respective fidelity. **'''''Attack Type''''': Determines the attack type of the hitbox, and therefore its counterability and adaptability. There are 5 attack types as of now, Melee, Bullet, Explosion, Swarm, and Domain. Consider that the attack type determines how counterable something is. **'''''Blockable''''': Targets can remain unaffected by the hitbox if they block and face the attack if this setting is on. **'''''360 Block''''': If the previous setting is enabled, the user only has to block without worrying about where they face to be unaffected. **'''''Cancel Enemy''''': The target's actions will be interrupted once they are affected by the hitbox if this setting is on. **'''''Clear Knockback''''': Targets will stand up once affected by the hitbox while ragdolled if this setting is on. **'''''Can Kill''''': The hitbox's damage can be lethal to targets if this setting is on. **'''''Hit Ragdoll''''': The hitbox can hit ragdolled players if this setting is on. **'''''Hit User''''': The hitbox can affect the user if this setting is on. **'''''Single Target''''': The hitbox can affect multiple targets if this setting is off. **'''''Branch''''': Chooses a branch to trigger on the user if a target is affected by the hitbox. **'''''Branch Target''''': Chooses a branch that will trigger specifically for any target affected by the hitbox. **'''''Branch Finisher''''': Chooses a branch that will trigger specifically when a target is killed by the hitbox. ***This will apply the branch to the user, and will be performed if any humanoid hit by this hitbox has (damage amount) health left after hit. **'''''Projectile Tag''''': Attaches the hitbox to a projectile with the same Projectile Tag. **'''''Link User''''': If another player hits the hit box with their hit box, they transfer all damage, stun, ragdoll, etc. to the user as if the user was standing instead of the hit box. (basically, a hitbox.) |- |
'''Branch'''
| *Branches act like groups of nodes, accessible as tabs above the skill builder's own tabs. These branches are intended to be parts belonging to the same custom move, yet each part is able to trigger once its conditions are fulfilled (mainly added to interact with Hit Cancels, but can work in tandem with [[Build Mode/Skill Builder#Conditions|conditions]]). A branch can be added by: #Placing its node on the default branch then naming it. #Adding its name on top of the skill builder menu. *After adding 2 branches, the user can then design two different moves with different conditions, but occupying the same custom move and acting as its variants by putting the branch nodes on the default branch. *Additionally, several other nodes can interact with branches, triggering them when certain conditions are fulfilled depending on the node. *Note that Properties cannot be changed as of now, and any changes to them will be global across all branches. **'''''Branch''''': Chooses a branch to trigger when the node is reached on the timeline. **'''''Random''''': Instead of going to a specific branch, the node will randomly select one of the inputted branches to start. Must separate branch names by "," without spaces ("A,B,C"). |- |
'''Visual'''
| *Creates a customized visual effect for a set amount of time once the node is reached on the timeline, and according to the following settings: **'''''Effects''''': Offers a wide array of visual effects that will preview on the user when clicked: Cancel, Overlay, Shake Light, Clash, Melee Trail, Beams, Wind Streak, Star, Mesh, Light, Billboard, Wind Expand, 360 Wind, Whirl Slash, Camera, Beam, Circle Glow, Flames, Distortion, Star Outline, Afterimage2, Field Of View, Cylinder, Black Flash, Energy Sparks, Cleave, Blood, Block, Ring, Burst, Sparks, Mass Hit, Wedge, Shake Heavy, Slash, Cursed Energy, Dismantle, Rough Energy, Screen Color, Sphere, Weak Lightning, Wind Ring, Shine, Shake Medium, Visibility, Glow. ***Some effects won't work without the proper settings, such as "Dismantle" and "Mass hit" requiring a Position and Alt Position to appear. **'''''Amount''''': Determines the amount of the effect that will spawn once the node is activated, unless the chosen effect is: **Field Of View, in which case this setting will determine the user's viewing distance, zooming away from the player the higher the amount. A negative amount will zoom towards the player's face. ***Mesh, in which case this setting is used to input a Mesh ID retrieved from the [https://create.roblox.com/store/meshparts Roblox Creator Store] **'''''Texture''''': Can be used to envelop the effect in a texture using a Texture ID retrieved from the [https://create.roblox.com/store/meshparts Roblox Creator Store]. This is only compatible with the Overlay, Billboard, and Mesh effects. **'''''Color''''': Determines the color that taints the effect once it appears. Defaulted to 255, 255, 255. **'''''Alt Color ''''': Determines the color that the effect will gradually shift to until it disappears, or simply a secondary color depending on the effect. Defaulted to 255, 255, 255 **'''''Opacity''''': Determines how transparent the effect is, where 1 is fully invisible and 0 is fully visible. **'''''Alt Opacity''''': Determines the transparency that the effect will gradually shift to until it disappears. **'''''Position''''': Determines the position of the effect depending on the user's own position using coordinates on the XYZ axis, where X is horizontal (left/right), Y is vertical (up/down), and Z is depth (forward/back), all in studs. **'''''Alt Position''''': Determines the position that the effect will end up in once it disappears, also depending on the user's own position. **'''''Rotation (R, Y, P)''''': Determines the rotation of the effect depending on the user's own rotation using roll (like a cartwheel), yaw (like a turn) and pitch (like a somersault). **'''''Alt Rotation (R, Y, P)''''': Determines the rotation that the effect will have once it disappears, also depending on the user's own rotation. **'''''Size''''': The size of the effect, as a multiplier. Defaulted to 1. **'''''Alt Size''''': Determines the size that the effect will have once it disappears. Also defaulted to 1. **'''''Time''''': Controls how long the effect will last for, therefore altering the speed of other settings. **'''''Last Hit''''': Determines how long the effect will use the position and rotation of the target they last attacked for reference rather than the user. Defaulted to -1 and recommended to be the same value as Time. **'''''Limb''''': Picks the center of the effect: HumanoidRootPart, Head, Torso, Right Arm, Left Arm, Right Leg, and Left Leg. Defaulted to HumanoidRootPart, which is the same as torso but without accounting for animations and such. **'''''Visual Tag''''': Works in tandem with the "Cancel" effect to remove all visual effects coming from nodes with the same Visual Tag ID and on the same limb. **'''''Projectile Tag''''': Attaches the effect to a projectile with the same Projectile Tag. (Obs.: to make this work properly, make sure the Projectile node is before [upper] the Visual node.) **'''''Run On Server''''': Makes the visual run the same for all players (server sided) rather than differently for each player (client sided), which will keep it from being overridden if it's still active after too many effects have played. This also makes the effect visible for newer players. **'''''Cancel On Interrupt''''': Removes the effect if the custom ability gets interrupted. **'''''Relative From Branch''''': Determines if the visual effect stay relative to the user rather than the target if applied through a "Branch Target" setting from another node. **'''''Easing Style''''': Lists several forms of mathematical functions (Linear, Sine, Quad, Cubic, Exponential, Back) that will dictate how the visual effect will accelerate, meaning how its speed will increase up as time goes. For example, a "Linear" style will maintain a constant speed throughout the animation, while an "Exponential" style gradually in slow at the beginning before a sudden sky-rocket in speed. The graphs for these functions can be seen [https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/enums/EasingStyle here] (all are shown the "In" direction) **'''''Easing Direction''''': Controls the direction of the function's curve, which defines when the acceleration occurs. Basically how the visual effect's speed fades: ***'''In''': Starts slowly and gradually speeds up. ***'''Out''': Starts fast and speeds down (decelerates) at the end. ***'''InOut''': Combines both In and Out, starting and ending slowly with a faster middle phase. |- |
'''Grab'''
| *Detects if damage was dealt to a target before sticking one of their body parts to the user's. **'''''Limb''''' and '''''Target Limb''''': Determines the body part that will be grabbing/grabbed: HumanoidRootPart, Head, Torso, Right Arm, Left Arm, Right Leg, and Left Leg. Defaulted to HumanoidRootPart (same as torso but independant of animations). **'''''Position''''': Determines the position of the target's limb depending on the user's limb using coordinates on the XYZ axis, where X is horizontal (left/right), Y is vertical (up/down), and Z is depth (forward/back), all in studs. **'''''Rotation (R, Y, P)''''': Determines the rotation of the target's limb depending on the user's limb using roll (like a cartwheel), yaw (like a turn) and pitch (like a somersault). **'''''Time''''': Determines how long the grab will last for. **'''''Last Hit''''': Determines how long the user has to damage/stun a target in order to apply the grab. Defaulted to 1. |- |
'''Projectile'''
| *Creates a moving hitbox, able to travel from one place to another. **'''''Projectile Tag''''': Allows the user to add effects from other nodes that will accompany the moving projectile by adding the same tag on a Visual, Hitbox, or Sound node. This will make these aforementioned nodes use the projectile as a reference rather than the user. **'''''Position''''': Determines the starting position of the projectile using coordinates on the XYZ axis, where X is horizontal (left/right), Y is vertical (up/down), and Z is depth (forward/back), all in studs and defaulted to 0, 0, 4. **'''''Rotation''''': Determines the rotation and therefore trajectory of the projectile, using roll, yaw, and pitch, defaulted to 0, 0, 0. **'''''Size''''': Determines the dimensions of the hitbox, where X is width, Y is height, and Z is depth, all in studs and defaulted to 6. **'''''Speed''''': How fast the projectile will move forward in studs, defaulted to 1. **'''''Time''''': How long the projectile will move forward in seconds before disappearing, defaulted to 1. **'''''Stun''''': Interrupts the targets' actions and stuns them for a chosen duration in seconds once they're affected by the projectile. **'''''Stun Anim''''': Forces targets hit by the projectile to perform the default stun animation when on, off by default. **'''''Damage''''': Damages the targets by a chosen amount once they're affected by the projectile. **'''''Debree''''': Determines if breakable objects within range of the projectile can be destroyed. The number determines the size of the debris in studs. Having any Debree over 0 will allow it to harm domains. **'''''Attack Type''''': Determines the attack type of the projectile, and therefore its counterability and adaptability. There are 5 attack types as of now, all available on this setting: Melee (counterable by everything), Bullet (counterable by some), Explosion (uncounterable), Swarm (uncounterable), and Domain (uncounterable, no matter what). **'''''Blockable''''': Targets can remain unaffected by the projectile if they block if this setting is on. **'''''360 Block''''': Targets can remain unaffected by the projectile if they block even while not facing the projectile if this setting is on along with the previous one. **'''''Cancel Enemy''''': The target's actions will be interrupted once they are affected by the projectile if this setting is on. **'''''Clear Knockback''''': Targets will stand up once affected by the projectile while ragdolled if this setting is on. **'''''Can Kill''''': The projectile's damage can be lethal to targets if this setting is on. **'''''Hit Ragdoll''''': The projectile can hit ragdolled players if this setting is on. **'''''Hit User''''': The projectile can affect the user if this setting is on. Unlike the "Add Health" node, the projectile's damage can kill the user if "Can Kill" is on. **'''''Single Target''''': The projectile can affect multiple targets if this setting is on. **'''''Aim Last Hit''''': Aims the projectile at a target hit in the last (value) seconds, **'''''Continue''''': Determines if the projectile dissipates/ends once it collides with a target if on, or if it pierces them and ends once '''''Time''''' is over if off. **'''''Branch''''': Chooses a branch to trigger on the user if a target is affected by the projectile. **'''''Branch Target''''': Chooses a branch that will trigger specifically on any target affected by the projectile. **'''''Branch Collided''''': Chooses a branch that will trigger specifically for the projectile when it collides with an obstacle. **'''''Filter Interval''''': Determines how long the projectile has to wait before it is able to affect the same target it just hit. Defaulted to 1. |- |
'''Tag'''
| *"Tags" are variables that are able to latch onto a player for a chosen period of time. This node will mark the user with a tag, or check if they have that same tag when this node is reached on the timeline. Currently, tags can be used to trigger branches when a check finds a tag of equal value, or to activate abilities with a set "Variant Tag" property. This node has several settings that allow it to interact with this variable in many ways: **'''''Tag''''': Determines the tag that will mark the user. **'''''Value''''': Determines how much value the tag will have, obtain, or the value that will be checked for, depending on the other settings. **'''''Time''''': Determines how long the tag will mark the user for. Once the duration is over, the tag will become null/inactive. **'''''Check''''': Determines if the node checks the value of a tag instead of marking the user with one. If the value of the tag is equal to the one set on '''''Value''''', the designated branch will start. This setting is prioritised over '''''"Add/Remove"''''' and '''''"Set"'''''. **'''''Add/Remove''''': Will add '''''Value''''' to the value of detected tags if "Add" is toggled on, or will nullify/deactivate the tag entirely if "Remove" is toggled on instead. **'''''Set''''': Will instead set the tag's value to the one inputted on the '''''Value''''' setting if both '''''Add''''' and this setting are toggled on. **'''''Branch''''': Placing a branch's name here will switch over to that branch when the '''''Check''''' detects a compatible tag. If last hit is set to a real value, the user will still proceed to the branch, instead of the last hit. ***This is good if you want the user to perform a branch if a target has a specific tag **'''''Last Hit''''': Determines how long the user can apply the tag to the target they last attacked. Defaulted to -1. |- |
'''Particle Emitter'''
| *Emits particles and such. **'''''Projectile Tag''''': When the name of an existing projectile's tag is given, sets the emitter's origin to said particle, rather than a limb. **'''''Last Hit''''': Activates the node on the target hit in the last (value) seconds. **'''''Part Size''''': Makes a part with the given size. (X, Y, Z) ***Use (0, 0, 0) to use attachments. **'''''Texture''''': The texture, such as a sprite or flipbook image. ***Determined by a TextureID. **'''''Emit Count''''': Amount of particles to spawn at once, only if '''''Duration''''' is set to (0). **'''''Rate''''': Particles spawned per second. ***Only active if '''''Duration''''' is more than 0. **'''''Duration''''': The amount of time, in seconds, that the emitter stays enabled. ***If 0, rely on '''''Emit Count'''''. **'''''Color''''': '''''ColorSequence''''' in Roblox. ***A cubic gradient defined by (r,g,b r,g,b ...). ***The tooltip in-game implies only 3 are possible, however upon testing, I could distinguish 7 colors from a 7-tone gradient. ***Recommend that you have a tool that puts them together for you, typing in the field is buggy upon a certain amount of characters. **'''''Size''''': '''''NumberSequence''''' in Roblox. ***Values separated by commas (size1, size2, size3...). ***Name is self-explanatory. **'''''Brightness''''': Determines how "emissive" the particle is when the Light Emmision property is >0 **'''''Transparency''''': '''''NumberSequence''''' in Roblox. ***Values separated by commas (alpha1, alpha2, alpha3...). ***0 is fully visible, 1 is invisible. **'''''Squash''''': '''''NumberSequence''''' in Roblox. ***Values separated by commas (squash1, squash2, squash3...). ***Vertical stretching. The higher the value, the thinner and taller the particle becomes; negative values will squish the particle. **'''''Lifetime''''': A random value between (a, b) to determine how long a particle lives for. ***This will max out at 20. **'''''Speed''''': A random value between (a, b) to determine the initial speed of a particle. **'''''Rotation''''': A random value between (a, b) to determine the initial rotation of a particle's texture. **'''''Rot Speed''''': A random value between (a, b) that determines the rotation speed of a particle's textures. ***Based off of observations, initial rotation is affected. **'''''Acceleration''''': The particle will accelerate over time according to the given Vector3. (x,y,z) ***Setting the Y value to a negative number can imitate the feeling of the particle(s) being affected by physics. **'''''Drag''''': Slows down the particle over time, larger values result in greater slowing. ***Setting this value to to a negative value will instead accelerate the particle over time. **'''''Light Emission''''': Determines if the particle "glows", from 0-1. **'''''Light Influence''''': Determines if the particle is influenced by lights, shadows, etc, from 0-1. Setting this to 1 is good for emissive particles. **'''''ZOffset''''': Determines the particle(s) Z axis rendered local the camera. ***For example, setting this to -2 will make the particles render behind the character, whilst with 2, will make the particles render infront of the character. **'''''Spread Angle''''': A Vector3 (x,y,z) that determines the spread of the particle, only the X&Y axes are needed. **'''''Position''''': Determines the relative offset of the ParticleEmitter to it's parent **'''''Lock To Part''''':If on, the particles will be connected/welded with it's parent **'''''Limb:''''': Determines which limb will be the ParticleEmitter's parent. **'''''Orientation Type''''': Determines how the particle will be orientated. The options are as followed: ***FacingCamera: The particle will face the camera, like a Nextbot in Garry's Mod. ***FacingCameraWorldUp: The particle will face the camera, but not on the Y axis. ***VelocityParallel: The particle's y-axis will face it's velocity. ***VelocityPerpendicular: The particle's z-axis will face it's velocity. **'''''Emission Direction''''': A list of six directions that determines the direction the particle will emit from. **'''''Flipbook Size''''': A Vector2 that determines how the particle's sprite will be split. (like 4,4 for a 4x4 spritesheet.) **'''''Flipbook Mode''''': Determines how the particle "flips", the list is as followed: ***Loop: The particle's spritesheet will loop indefinitely. ***OneShot: The particle's spritesheet will play once, then end. Useful for explosions or one-time effects. (frame-rate is determined by lifetime) ***PingPong: The particle's spritesheet will loop oscillationally indefinitely. (back and forth) ***Random: The particle's spritesheet will alter between random sprites indefinitely. **'''''Flipbook Framerate''''': Determines how fast the spritesheet will play, in terms of FPS. Though this is a Vector2, so I'm not sure if it's randomized from a-b, or is just a Vector2 for no reason. **'''''Emitter Shape''''': Determines the "shape" or volume of the ParticleEmitter, which also determines the orienation of each particle. The list is as followed: ***Box: The particles will spawn within a boundary of a Vector3. ***Cylinder: The particles will spawn radially on the x&z axis, but globally on the Y axis. ***Disc: Fill this out later ***Sphere: The particles will spawn within radially from all axes. **'''''Emitter Shape Inout''''': Fill this out later. **'''''Shape Partial''''': Fill this out later. **'''''Run on Server''''': If on, the ParticleEmitter will be instantiated serversided, meaning that new players will see the ParticleEmitter. **'''''Client Sided''''': If on, the ParticleEmitter will be instantiated only on the target's client, making only them see it. **'''''Cancel Tag''''': The cancel tag linked to the ParticleEmitter (string) **'''''Cancel''''': If on, will cancel any ParticleEmitters with the same Cancel Tag **'''''Cancel on Interrupt''''': If on, the ParticleEmitter will cancel if the move is interrupted or cancelled. |- |
'''Add Health'''
| *'''''Amount''''': Adds the chosen amount of health to the user, with the default value being 5. **Inputting a negative value will instead take that amount away from the user. *'''''Can Kill''''': Kills the player when the lost health is usually lethal. Off by default. |- |
'''Hit Cancel'''
| *Will check if the user has dealt any stun or damage before this node is reached in the timeline. If yes, then then the rest of the custom move be will canceled immediately. **'''''Time''''': Dictates the time frame before the Hit Cancel was reached in the timeline that will be checked for stun (Hit Cancel will check for stun dealt in the past Time). Defaulted to 1 second. **'''''Flip''''': Reverses Hit Cancel's behavior, instead canceling the custom move if no stun or damage was dealt when it is on. Otherwise, it cancels the move if stun was dealt when it is off. **'''''Endlag''''': Forces the user to freeze after the custom move is canceled, for a chosen amount of time defaulted to 1 second. **'''''Branch''''': Instead of simply ending the move, the Hit Cancel is able to start the selected branch's timeline. |- |
'''Loop'''
| *Repeats a specific number of nodes above it when this node is reached in the timeline. **'''''Loop Back''''': The amount of nodes it'll loop back. Defaulted to 1. **'''''Loop Amount''''': The amount of times this node will loop. Defaulted to 3. **'''''Hold''''': Dictates whether or not the node(s) above it are looped as long as the skill is held. |- |
'''Set Melee'''

move/running distance |} |-|Tips and Tricks= Here is a list of tips and tricks one can use when making custom skills or as inspiration, for added shenanigans. ===General=== *When using grab, the victim of the grab will become invulnerable to damage, this can be bypassed by using the Add Health node to decrease or increase the victim's hp. While this cant kill them normally, you can turn the can kill toggle on in the add health node, or add a Branch node at the end that checks if the user has a low amount of health, and if so, kills the victim using a hitbox node. *You can make a cartoony explosion effect by adding a Clash effect, setting its color to a constant (255, 128, 64), and then setting both the alt opacity and alt size to 10. *Idol's Debut normally forces you to move up to the victim to kick them to the ground. However, if you add a wait node for 0.25s, and then add Resolute Slash after the wait node, you will be able to turn around and bluetooth-kick the enemy downwards. Do note that this is best used out of awakening, as cutscenes seen in Climax Jumping and Idol's Debut only appear in awakening, and it will make it hard to aim precisely with Bluetooth Debut. *When making a blockable custom move that starts with an unblockable skill, you can add a hitbox block as well as a Hit Cancel node that ends the move if it did not hit. If the blockable hitbox dealt stun (aka was not blocked), then you can cancel it and have the rest of the skill continue after it. *Use the default branch as the hub to connect other branches two to help solve the problem of "branchlag" that comes from branches playing inside of the custom move and not being considered separate. For example, adding a ground and air variant can be done with a branch hub connecting them. Simply add a false air conditional to the air variant, and a true air conditional to the ground variant. Add the air variant branch block before the ground variant branch block inside the hub. *The colors for cursed energy are blue (85, 170, 255), pink (245, 105, 255), purple (170, 85, 255), darker purple (111, 67, 255), green (85, 255, 127), and red (255, 110, 110). *Using Lapse Blue MAX on Flash Freezing's frames is the only way to reliably make an custom move that has Unlimited Purple. **Do note that you cannot cancel Flash Freezing midway to spawn less frames, as it will always summon 15 frames no matter what. *The visual stun effect can be replicated by adding a Glow effect with opacity 0.8, alt opacity 1, 0.15s of time, and 0.9 size. *Using the new look node you can create flight without top speed. By putting a look and setting the time value to how much you like, with a smoothness anywhere between 150 and 200, with grounded and camera direction on, and a velocity node that lasts the same time of the look then set the force (0,1,75), set track on and add a wait at the end set the time of the wait the same of the velocity and look to make a flight move. *The frames in Head of the Hei's Flash Freezing move are actually their own rigs, which you can apply branches to. * *The following collapsible contains an import code that simulates Mahoraga's Ritual drain passive. Keep in mind that regaining awakening meter must be done using the "Add Awakening" node.

*Most visual effects that have relative positioning (attached/move with the player, e.g Mesh, Wind Streak, Whirl Slash) can be turned into VFX with absolute (doesn't move with the player) positioning by adding an Alt Position. *You can create an air variant move like Execution or Mass Breaker by using a look node, placing a velocity block (0, 0.1, 0) for however long you want to stay in the air before adding your rush velocity (0, 0.1, X) the X can be changed to how far and fast you want to travel. ===Cancel Tricks=== *By launching the enemy upwards then using Fluttering Pounce with Revolve at the same time and canceling both right after, the enemy will stay suspended in the air. *Canceling Cursory Impact after 0.06 seconds will apply an afterimage effect on you. ===Speed Tricks=== *Putting Rush on 0 speed will disable movement and lock your rotation in-place, meaning you cannot turn or move your character even by shiftlocking, and you can enable rotation and movement back by canceling it. *By setting a skill's speed to any number over 10,000, you can trigger a variant/finisher of the skill after the base skill has ended (Note: The new "Start" property can do the same if you fiddle around with it): **Bleedout's finisher will trigger, turning your screen blue and adding projection afterimages to you. **If the target of a custom skill is forced to preform a branch (last hit) with Resolute Slash (must include teleport) in it, they will disappear once they try teleporting. (Literally, they will VANISH from existence and respawn instantly.) (This also works for Takedown and Limitless!) **In Head Splitter's case and a majority of other counters, the counter will automatically trigger. **Idol's Debut and Climax Jumping will instantly trigger the last attack. Good for powerful hits. **Do note that when using a move at extremely high speeds, sometimes its' animation glitches out and can play well after the custom move has actually ended. To stop this, add the animation that the move uses after it (any part/speed works! just make sure to add the animation), and if you wish, immediately add another custom animation right after to cancel it, making it appear as if there were no animation residue in the first place. *To force an awakening outfit to activate using a skill or special, use Time Cell Moon Palace at 0 speed then immediately cancel it. This will apply the awakening outfit without casting the domain expansion, or even triggering its popup. ===Other=== *[https://ossaamm.github.io/ Here] is a link to a website full of '''skill timings''' and in-game '''sounds'''. *If a base character with cosmetics (i.e. [[Honored One]]'s blindfold) is chosen, they can be hidden by hiding the HumanoidRootPart using Visibilty in a Visual node, placing a short wait afterwards, and then individually showing each limb using the same method. Not all cosmetics are guaranteed to get hidden. ==Current Issues== *This section was added to notify users of the many issues that players can come across: *Rika's Full Manifestation cant be acessed if the Cursed Partners is with a custom awakening *All custom abilities show delay/lag when they are first used. And the only way to fix them is to use the moves. Several skills and specials are either broken themselves or cause the custom move itself to break: **Some moves still play sounds after being cancelled (Body Disfigure, Open FURNACE, Plasma Wave, Strong Dismantle variants, etc..) **Rika is required for all of her moves (Rika Downslam, True Love Beam, Rika Slam..). While she can still be summoned within the custom move to perform them, she cannot be desummoned. **Specials do not have a "Hold For" setting, and therefore one Mass Buildup node will not charge the Mass Bar, as least 4 are needed. Be aware that {{Star Rage}}'s charged variants do not require the Mass Bar to be implemented in a custom move, so doing that is unnecessary if you just want the charged variants. *Hit Cancel can register stun dealt outside of the custom move (by another move, M1s, etc), but only if the "Time" setting goes beyond the custom move's startup. **Setting a WAIT that lasts for the duration of the first move's startup/counter window before the Hit Cancel should fix this issue, but only if Hit Cancel's "Time" is set to the same duration. **A second WAIT is also required to be set after Hit Cancel. *The capture unit only works if there is a wait in front of it. *The SOUND node's "Fade Out" is currently broken at the moment. *A custom special's cooldown will switch upon using Awakening (it will switch to said awakening's special cooldown). *The Grab node will bug out and teleport the user to their target if the ability ends before it registers stun. **An example of this is a single Grab node by itself, but this can be fixed by adding a WAIT node for the duration of the grab. *Applying a LOOK block on a dummy or NPC will cause the rig to disappear/delete. * You can "variant hop" SKILL blocks by changing the START property to the respective variant (such as ~2 seconds on Dismantle for an instant WCS.) ** Nonetheless, setting the SPEED property to 1000+ will simultaneously perform all variants of that move at once, including finishers. ** You can also use the variant hopping technique for counters; setting the START property to ~1 for Manji Kick will skip to the Manji Kick's kick * Some target moves like Resolute Slash and Mahoraga applies LAST HIT to targets even if they have i-frames. * You can make a HITBOX or PROJECTILE uncounterable by decoding the moveset data, going into the node's JSON data, changing the ATTACK TYPE property to a string like "Infinity" or anything else, reimport the data, then import that data onto your character. * Moves will become more laggier/delayed the more of the map is destroyed.

==Notes== *As of now, the only achievement to grant a reward is "The strongest of history", which gives the "Phenomenal" Victory Flash upon completion. *The "Truly Innocent" achievement is rewarded to every player but the domain caster upon the fifth confession without a guilty verdict. This means the achievement can be earned by invading the domain right before the fifth confession. *The "Perfect Block Garuda Rebound variants 15 times" weekly quest refers to the Charged Garuda Rebound variant, and not the regular use twice variant. *The "Adapt to all damage types fully at least once as [[Mahoraga]]" quest must be done without dying. *The "Obtain Jackpot 15 times in a row without dying as {{Restless Gambler}}" and "Awaken 5 times with [[Mahoraga]]" do not work at all. *Every achievement or quest that requires players to be hit by trains can be contributed to by hitting yourself with the train. *The daily quest for using specials 15 times cannot be progressed by switching stances. *The achievement "Red hasn't exploded yet.." contains a typo, where Reversal Red is misspelled as Reserval. __NOTOC__
