I survive!|Haruta Shigemo ({{Lucky Coward}})}} ==Description== Lucky Coward is the 18th [[Characters|character]] and 4th [[Characters#Base Only|base-only]] that was added to ''Jujutsu Shenanigans''. ===Origin=== {{Origin |Lucky Coward is based off of {{Jjk|Haruta Shigemo}}, a character from ''Jujutsu Kaisen''. |{{Jjk|Haruta Shigemo}} is a minor antagonist and curse user who sided with Kenjaku. Despite his lack of skill in combat and even his unawareness of how his own "Miracles" technique worked, which is by saving daily fortuitous events and erasing them from his memory so they can be expended to survive otherwise fatal blows, Haruta proved to still be a danger, although he openly admits to being cowardly and prefers targeting weak opponents, thus the title: "Lucky Coward". }} ==Moveset== |-|Base= {{Ability |Name='''Shoot!''' |Type=COSMETIC/PASSIVE |Type Color=darkviolet |Description=Since the user isn't experienced enough to fight using their fists, they hold a cursed tool resembling a katana blade connected to a humanoid hand.

Consequently, their final basic attack will deal extra damage as it punctures the target's torso when landed (uppercuts and downslams excluded), and their front dash is able to kick away grounded ragdolled opponents. |Stat 1=EFFECT |Stat 1 Value=Increases final M1 damage by 1, and allows Front Dashes to bypass ragdoll |Image=Shoot!.gif}} {{Ability |Name='''Miracles''' |Type=PASSIVE |Type Color=purple |Description=Above the user's Awakening Bar lie six triangles, each able to fill up by storing a "miracle" that the user can later utilize in many ways: *Upon a supposed death, the user's cursed technique will automatically activate and consume 3 miracles to keep the user alive by setting their HP to 12.5. **Within a second of expending 3 miracles to survive a fatal hit, any attack that would kill the user will cost them one miracle to survive rather than 3. *The user can also manually use their miracles to ragdoll cancel if they lack enough escape meter. However, this will drain any meter they built up before evading. The user always starts out with three stored miracles, but is able to gain a miracle by: *Landing a dodge while unarmed. *Performing a full taunt on a standing enemy. *Interrupting an enemy's action or hitting an enemy impaired by Jawbreaker with the first three M1s, Ambush, Backstab, or Trip. |Stat 1=EFFECT |Stat 1 Value=Allows the user to ragdoll cancel or survive death using 3 miracles |Image=Miracles.gif}} {{Ability |Name='''Miracle''' |Type=PASSIVE |Type Color=purple |Description=While unarmed, pressing the block button will prepare the user to evade any incoming melee or bullet attack, hinted by a circle effect around them. A successful dodge will put this ability on a reduced cooldown, while disabling Ankle Cutter and High Time for 0.3s while rewarding the user with a miracle. |Stat 1=EFFECT |Stat 1 Value=Changes blocking to a 360∘ bullet dodge with a 0.25s window and a cooldown going from 1s to 0.15s if landed |Image=Miracle.gif}} {{Ability |Name='''Taunt''' |Type=PASSIVE |Type Color=purple |Unblockable=y |Interruptible=y |Cannot Bypass Ragdoll=y |Description=The user's basic attack is also removed while unarmed. the sword will slice off the left arm of any victims in its way. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 1 Value=Insta-kill |Stat 2=COOLDOWN |Stat 2 Value=15s |Image=DirtyPlayFinisher.gif}} ==Pros & Cons== {{ProsCons |pros= *Moderate damage with low cooldowns, mostly using puppet attacks which keep the pressure on the opponent. *Great against passive players that hold block and keep their distance as you can taunt them to gain miracles, countering with Ankle Cutter and High Time if they decide to attack. *Miracles are best used as extra evasives, allowing you to easily escape combos over and over. *Can dodge most attacks infinitely, and counter using Trip or by ordering the sword to attack. *Can mixup with Backstab to get an extra M1 chain on unprepared enemies. *The awakening gives you 8 seconds to do whatever you want to the target, with them being completely unable to fight back. *You may use your Helping Hand abilities while stunned, allowing you to guarantee moves or combo. |cons= *65 Max HP is extremely low HP compared to other characters and some character's simple combos can deplete all HP. *The Hand Sword may get stuck on debris or get confused around terrain while tracking enemies. Additionally, its attacks are able to miss if the enemy is in constant movement. *Miracles can get wasted during combos, as the 12.5 HP you gain from them can be depleted quickly. *Lacks the offense to beat turtling opponents while unarmed. }} ==Combos== {{Combo |sequence1=---- |damage1='''''This character Combos are currently being reworked.
Please don't add any combos whatsoever.''''' |notes1=---- }} ==Tips & Techs== ===Tips=== *The Helping Hand sword acts as a separate entity from the user. This means that the user cannot get countered if Ankle Cutter and High Time get countered, as the counterattack will be directed to their sword. **This allows {{Switcher}}'s Boogie Woogie to interact with the sword, allowing players to swap with it. **{{Head of the Hei}} is also able to apply Projection Meter on the sword. *The second part of {{Salaryman}}'s Interrogate will require 6 miracles to survive instead of 3. *Timing Trip right before the target gets knocked away from Jawbreaker can redirect the knockback and allow you to reach the target easier. **If timed right, you're able to land a set of 3 M1s 4 times on an enemy before they're able to escape. *If you wait for your opponent to front dash into you, you can dodge and then use Trip to quickly get 2 miracles. *You can use Taunt on a ragdolled player, and if timed right, you can get a miracle right as they wake up. *Using a forward dash after a Cheap Shot will send your opponent closer to your blade, letting the weapon confirm High Time or Ankle Cutter quicker. *Backstab is a good mixup tool, but while landing it from behind allows you to begin combos easily, you cannot get a fully true M1 reset from it, even by dashing. The safest way to use it is on wakeup, or by simply relying on High Time instead. *All of Helping Hand’s moves can be used even after death, including the awakening and special, giving you the option to retaliate after you die. Though it will only work if you were unarmed before dying. *You can bypass being completely unarmed by using an [[Items|item]] weapon such as Jet Black, Naginata, Crowbar or Playful Cloud. However, you will not be able to taunt or block while unarmed. ===Techs=== |-|Beginner= ===='''Downslambush'''==== You can use Ambush's ragdoll variant once, and then M1 the air to land a true downslam on the victim before they get up. Does 2 less damage than using Ambush's ragdoll variant twice but allows for better combo extension. ===='''Upper-Torso Stab'''==== You can time an uppercut into backstab the only downside to this is it should be used as a combo ender due to the ragdoll from this. |-|Intermediate= ===='''Tripping Slam'''==== It's similar to Gojo's red downslam tech, except you can use it even if your opponent isn't ragdolled, and can use any amount of M1s. Mainly though, M1 your opponent once, use trip, then down slam them while they are tripped because they don't get knockback if they are not ragdolled when you use trip(also deals fall damage). You have to do it fast though so it could take practice. ===='''Insult to Injury'''==== After landing Backstab on an opponent's back, start walking back for about half a second, then front dash the opponent. This deals the same damage as High Time, and doesn't reset your M1s, but is better for when your opponent has their evasive. |-|Advanced= ===='''Backstab Reset 1'''==== After hitting a 3-m1 chain on an opponent, landing Backstab (back) a moment after they become green again will reset the m1 chain, allowing for extension. However, doing so requires very precise timing and mechanics, specially if you want to land it by side-dashing behind your opponent.
Needless to say, this tech is really risky since it can be easily countered and you can just get punched out of it and punished if you mess up. ===='''Backstab Reset 2''==== After landing an uppercut jump and use trip then quickly side dash and hit their back with backstab this will allow you to extend a combo. ===='''Anti-Counter Tech'''==== If you accidentally hit a counter, it's possible to drop Helping Hand with the special before being hit, allowing you to avoid getting punished. This is extremely difficult, however, as it requires split-second reaction time to pull off, but the benefits are truly worth it.
Keep in mind that dropping the sword requires you to not be stunned. Therefore, this tech is only possible against a select few counters that allow you to act before hitting you. These are {{Vessel}}'s Manji Kick, {{Restless Gambler}}'s Door Guard, {{Blood Manipulator}}'s Supernova and {{Aspiring Mangaka}}'s Eye Catching. ==Trivia== *{{Lucky Coward}} has the lowest HP in the entire game, although mitigated by miracles. *Stinger, Million Stab and High Time are references to moves from the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devil_May_Cry_(TV_series) Devil May Cry series]. *{{Lucky Coward}}'s 2026 April Fools Name (kind scholar) is based off of AniDiscourse's [https://www.youtube.com/shorts/HXe2nOlOaww "Scholar Haruta"] short. **These origins are shared with {{Salaryman}} (enjoys beating the life out of), {{Defense Attorney}} (greedy lawyer), {{Switcher}} (menace to society), {{Blood Manipulator}} (loving and caring brother) and {{Perfection}} (purifier). *By using No Stun, Cheap Shot and Dirty Play can switch up the passives you obtain when used twice really quickly, giving you either M1s and taunts, or taunts and block. *Dirty Play currently has a bug where if the sword flies into an opponent right as they catch you in a ragdolling move, the move will cancel and you'll continue to be ragdolled while slowly levitating up in the air for a few seconds. ==Gallery== File:HarutaAnime.png|Haruta Shigemo, the inspiration for Lucky Coward. ==History== To read about all of the character's changes, expand the collapsible below.

{| class="toc" style="background:#000000; border:1px solid #a2a9b1; padding:10px; width:350px;" |- ! style="font-size:120%; text-align:left;" | '''Table of Contents''' |- | style="font-size:95%;" | * [[#General|General]] * [[#Character Page Structure|Character Page Structure]] * [[#Character and Ability Templates|Character and Ability Templates]] * [[#PNG & GIF Formatting and Uploading Tutorial|PNG & GIF Formatting and Uploading Tutorial]] * [[#Character Page Template|Character Page Template]] * [[#Character Page Template Notes|Character Page Template Notes]] |}
This Manual of Style explains how to write and format pages on the ''Jujutsu Shenanigans Wiki''. All editors should read these guidelines before creating or substantially changing an article. If a page has no dedicated template, follow the structure of comparable existing pages. '''Before editing:''' Use [[Honored One]] as the baseline for character pages. Replace example text with verified information, preview the page, and contact a [[Wiki Staff|staff member]] if a new mechanic does not fit the current format. ==General== ===Writing and accuracy=== * Use correct grammar, spelling, and punctuation. Follow {{w|American and British English spelling differences|American English spelling}} consistently. * Write objectively in the third person. Use “the player” or “the user” instead of “you” in articles. * Keep personal opinions, jokes, immature wording, and unsupported claims out of articles. * Describe information available in the game. Do not add leaks, even if they come from in-game staff. * Correct inaccurate or outdated information when possible. If a detail cannot be verified, raise it with staff rather than presenting it as fact. ===Creating and maintaining pages=== * Create a new page when a major addition warrants its own article and is not already covered by an existing feature. * Keep related information together. For example, codes belong in a section on [[Shop]] rather than on a separate page. * Follow the current templates when creating pages or bringing older pages up to date. * Help correct vandalism and report vandals to [[Wiki Staff|staff]]. * Mistakes can be corrected. Use informative edit summaries and cooperate with other editors. ==Character Page Structure== Character pages should follow the section order below. Include optional forms and mechanics only when they apply to the character. {| class="fandom-table" style="width:100%;" ! Section ! Required content |- | Infobox and quote | Use the Character2 infobox for the character’s render, health, availability, awakening, special, and previous/next characters. Use a noob avatar with a torso matching the character’s special bar, awakening bar, or melee trail colors. Include an attributed quote when relevant. |- | Description | State the character’s availability or classification and its order of addition to the game. |- | Origin | Identify the character’s inspiration. Put backstory spoilers in the Origin template’s collapsible section. |- | Moveset | Use Ability cards for cosmetics, passives, specials, and moves. Separate the base moveset, awakenings, and finishers with tabs where applicable. |- | Pros & Cons | List specific combat strengths and weaknesses supported by the character’s mechanics. If the character is incomplete, state what is missing. |- | Combos | Show move/input sequences, damage, and relevant risks or conditions using the approved Combo format. |- | Tips & Techs | Separate general tips from techniques. Group techniques by Beginner, Intermediate, or Advanced difficulty and explain how to perform them. |- | Trivia | Include relevant development details, references, voicelines, soundtracks, and former features. |- | Gallery | Include an image of the character’s inspiration and other useful visuals, such as special interactions. |- | History | List additions, changes, and fixes in a collapsed update table. Place the Character Navigation template below it. |} ==Character and Ability Templates== ===Character infobox=== Use {{Character2}} for the infobox. Replace the placeholders, remove unused forms, and use the character’s colors for awakening and special names. ''Example code:'' 

{{Character2
|title1=Character Name
|image1=

Missingimage.jpeg|Base
Missingimage1.png|Awakening (if any)
Missingimage.jpeg|Second/Alternate Awakening (if any)

|hp=Health
|cost=Free/Early Access
|awakening=
*'''Awakening Name'''
*'''Second/Alternate Awakening Name'''
|special=
*'''Special'''
*'''Awakening Special''' (if different)
|previous=Previous / N/A
|next=Next / N/A
}}
'''Notes''' * Use descriptive image captions to distinguish the base form, awakening, and alternate awakening. * Match the existing character-page color treatment. Plain readable text is preferable to an effect that makes the name difficult to read. * Infobox placement is controlled by the wiki’s layout and may differ between desktop and mobile. * Contact staff if a new character’s forms or mechanics require changes to the template. ===Ability cards=== Use {{Ability}} for each ability. Default combat statistics are '''DAMAGE''', '''COOLDOWN''', and '''AWAKENING COST''' when applicable. Change statistic labels when another measurement better describes the mechanic, such as HEALING or DURATION. ''Example code:'' 

{{Ability
|Name=Special Name
|Type=SPECIAL
|Type Color=orange
|Perfect Blockable=y
|Uninterruptible=y
|Cannot Bypass Ragdoll=y
|No Lock On=y
|Description=Explain what the ability does and how it is used.
|Stat 1=DAMAGE
|Stat 1 Value=??
|Stat 2=COOLDOWN
|Stat 2 Value=??
|Stat 3=AWAKENING COST
|Stat 3 Value=??
|Image=Gif place holder.jpg
}}
''Rendered example:'' {{Ability |Name=Special Name |Type=SPECIAL |Type Color=orange |Perfect Blockable=y |Uninterruptible=y |Cannot Bypass Ragdoll=y |No Lock On=y |Description=Explain what the ability does and how it is used. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 1 Value=?? |Stat 2=COOLDOWN |Stat 2 Value=?? |Stat 3=AWAKENING COST |Stat 3 Value=?? |Image=Gif place holder.jpg }} ====Move types and colors==== ===Move Types, Colors, and Properties=== The {{Ability}} template uses the Type and Type Color parameters to display an ability's classification in the upper-right corner of the ability card. Move types and colors should remain consistent across all character pages. ====Move Types and Colors==== Set Type and Type Color using the following reference. {| class="fandom-table" style="width:100%;" ! Move classification ! Type ! Type Color |- | PASSIVE | PASSIVE | purple |- | COSMETIC | COSMETIC | mediumpurple |- | COSMETIC/PASSIVE | COSMETIC/PASSIVE | darkviolet |- | SPECIAL | SPECIAL | orange |- | SPECIAL VARIANT | SPECIAL VARIANT | orange |- | VARIANT | VARIANT | red |- | AWAKENING | AWAKENING | navy |- | DOMAIN AWAKENING | DOMAIN AWAKENING | black |- | TRUE AWAKENING | TRUE AWAKENING | royalblue |- | SUPER AWAKENING | SUPER AWAKENING | crimson |} For a base-only character's awakening move, use the label '''AWAKENING MOVE''' with the awakening color. Distinguish a domain awakening from a true awakening when the character can progress between these states. Describe the actual conditions and effects in the ability's description. ====Move Properties==== Move properties are displayed beneath an ability's description. To add a property, set its corresponding parameter to y. For example: 

|Perfect Blockable=y
|Total Armor=y
|Uninterruptible=y
|Cannot Bypass Ragdoll=y
|No Lock On=y
|Explosion=y
|Beam=y

Prepare the file=== * Crop the file cleanly and optimize it; aim for a file size under 10 MB. * PNGs should clearly show the relevant pose, moment, or hitbox. * GIFs should show the complete ability or technique from start to finish without unnecessary frames. * Use descriptive filenames, such as Honored_One_Base.png or Hanami_Root_Swarm_Visual_Cancel.gif. Avoid generic names such as RobloxScreenshot_273648.png. ===2. Upload the file=== Open [[Special:Upload]], select the PNG or GIF, and use a clear filename and description. ===3. Insert the file=== * Open the page in the editor and insert the uploaded image where it belongs. * In source editing, use the appropriate template image parameter or file markup. For example: 

[[File:Honored_One_Base.png|thumb|Honored One in its base form.]]
* Add a caption where it helps explain the image. Ability template image parameters should follow the format used in the examples above. ===4. ==Character Page Template Notes== ===Using the template=== * The code sample and rendered preview show the same structure. Copy the source rather than the rendered output. * Keep only the forms, moves, finishers, and mechanics that apply to the desired character. Duplicate an Ability card when more entries are needed. * Replace ??, example names, placeholder images, and category comments before publishing. * Use {{Jjk|Character Name}} when linking a Jujutsu Kaisen character through the wiki’s Jjk template. * Keep tooltip calls outside heading markup. Use a plain technique heading followed by the tooltip and written instructions. ===Combos=== * If you have a combo, please suggest it to a [[Wiki Staff#Content Moderator|Content Moderator]] rather than any other staff. * When making a combo, make sure the Damage Counter setting is on which can be toggled in [[Settings]]. * The skeleton uses the numbered Combo parameters shown in this manual: sequence1, damage1, and notes1. Follow the current [[Template:Combo|Combo template documentation]] for additional entries. * State relevant conditions, risks, and damage variations in the notes. ===History=== * Use [-] for a nerf, [/] for a neutral change, and [+] for a buff. * If an entry needs multiple markers, keep the order Nerf / Neutral / Buff and separate the applicable markers with a slash. * Describe what changed rather than adding opinions about the update. * Keep {{Character Navigation}} below the history table. ==References== When using the parameter, use the {{RefBox}} template right below the {{Character Navigation}} template to render all references on a page, instead of using . ===Reporting format problems=== If a new mechanic, template change, or layout issue makes this manual inaccurate, contact a [[Wiki Staff|staff member]] so the examples and instructions can be updated together.

[[Category:Characters]][[Category:Base Only Characters]] {{DISPLAYTITLE:'''Sky Bender'''}} {{Background|Skymanipbackground.webp}} {{Character2 |image1=SkyAssassin.png |hp=100 |title1={{Sky Bender}} |cost=Free |awakening='''Temper''' |special='''Sky Veil''' |previous={{Black Death}} |next={{Strongest Of History}}}} {{Quote|You Fujiwara are always in my way! Are you that afraid of me becoming somebody?!|Takako Uro ({{Sky Bender}}) to Yuta Okkotsu ({{Cursed Partners}})}} ==Description== Sky Bender is the 15th [[Characters#Early Access|Early Access]], 7th base only and 24th [[Characters|character]] that was added to Jujutsu Shenanigans. ===Origin=== {{Origin |Sky Bender is based off of {{Jjk|Takako Uro}}, a character from ''Jujutsu Kaisen''. |{{Jjk|Takako Uro}} is a jujutsu sorcerer from a thousand years ago who was reincarnated by {{Jjk|Kenjaku}} to participate in the Culling Game. Back in the Heian Era, Uro used to be the captain of a group of assassins called the Sun, Moon, and Stars Squad. That combined with her use of the Cursed Technique "Sky Manipulation" granted her the title: "Sky Bender".}} ==Moveset== |-|Base= {{Ability |Type=COSMETIC/PASSIVE |Type Color=darkviolet |Name='''Sky Manipulation''' |Description=Due to the user’s cursed technique, instead of walking they hover above the ground at all times. This also additionally affects their combat as: *Uppercuts have more knockback. *Within proximity of an airborne enemy, initiating the second basic attack will deliver a heavy downslam. **Whenever this M1 is blocked, and the target will begin winding up a heavy punch as a counterattack. Said punch is blockable, but will disable the user's ragdoll cancel and ground them for a long time. |Stat 1=EFFECT |Stat 1 Value=Increases uppercut knockback and allows M1s to combo midair |Image=SkyManipulation.gif}} {{Ability |Type=PASSIVE |Type Color=purple |Interruptible=y |Name='''Temper''' |Description=As the fight goes on, the user gets angrier and angrier with their opponent.

On the Awakening Bar, a "Temper" bar will build up as the user deals damage, filling up 4 times quicker than a regular awakening bar. However, not dealing any damage in the last 15 seconds will cause the Temper built up to be lost at a rate of 5% every half a second.

When full, pressing the Awakening button will prompt the user to shatter 2 distortions behind them, then yelling "Are you that afraid?". Following this, the user's head will start visibly smoking from rage, and they will be placed into an enhanced state: *All active cooldowns will be shortened to 3 seconds unless they were shorter than that. *All moves but Turbulence will feature notable improvements, but the user will be unable to build up any Temper or Awakening whatsoever. *All basic attacks will be able to initiate and extend air combos in a similar manner to the second M1, which will now have different knockback. *Front dashing with a ragdolled target in sight will send the user flying in the direction they aimed in. |Stat 1=EFFECT |Stat 1 Value=Builds up temper, which requires ~71.5 damage to enter an empowered state lasting for 15 seconds |Image=Temper.gif}} {{Ability |Type=SPECIAL |Type Color=orange |Name='''Sky Veil''' |Description=The user quickly spins around while holding a distortion to cover themselves up with it, making them invisible to the naked eye. Keep in mind that while invisible, they cannot perform any action other than walking, which will feature an increased speed.
This state will last for 2 seconds but can be canceled early using the special or a skill. However, the user will experience some endlag at the end unless they became visible within 30 studs of an enemy, or used a skill to cancel the state. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 2=AWAKENING COST |Stat 3=COOLDOWN |Stat 3 Value=8s |Image=SkyVeil.gif}} {{Ability |Name='''Blind Rage''' |Unblockable=y |Interruptible=y |Cannot Bypass Ragdoll=y |Melee=y |Description=The user winds up a quick grab by surging forwards with their cursed technique. If successful, they will choke their target and fly 125 studs with them before tossing them away.

If the target evades out of the grab while above 25 studs of altitude, they will automatically perform the air combo's counterattack on the user. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 1 Value=5 for grab, 4 for toss |Stat 2=COOLDOWN |Stat 2 Value=15s |Image=BlindRage.gif}} {{Ability |Type=VARIANT |Type Color=red |Name='''Blind Rage''' |Semi Blockable=y |Interruptible=y |Cannot Bypass Ragdoll=y |Melee=y |Description=While in Temper, the user will throw two blockable swings before following up with their usual grab attempt, which will feature an extra second of flight time if the user crashed into a surface.

These swings are will affect the surfaces near the user, giving them the ability to redirect incoming projectiles away from the user. However, the swings will not move the user forwards if blocked, and if an airborne ragdolled enemy is near, the user will hover to them and immediately skip to the grab. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 1 Value=3 per punch, 5 for grab, 4 for toss |Stat 2=COOLDOWN |Stat 2 Value=15s |Image=BlindRageTemper.gif}} {{Ability |Name='''Sky Distortion''' |Blockable=y |Interruptible=y |Cannot Bypass Ragdoll=y |Melee=y |Bullet Armor=y |Description=The user spins while holding onto the atmosphere in front of them, using its surface to launch any enemy they walk into. The distortion is able to redirect any incoming deflectable projectiles towards the direction faced by the user, who will gain i-frames exclusively against bullet attacks for roughly 0.7 seconds.

Using the move while airborne will cause the user to suddenly dash 20 studs forwards during their spin. If blocked, the user will be set face to face with their target. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 1 Value=10 |Stat 2=COOLDOWN |Stat 2 Value=12s |Image=SkyDistortion.gif}} {{Ability |Type=VARIANT |Type Color=red |Name='''Sky Distortion''' |Semi Blockable=y |Interruptible=y |Semi Ragdoll=y |Melee=y |Bullet=y |Description=While in Temper, the user will send the distortion forwards after their spin ends, which will act as a quick projectile bypassing both block and ragdoll that will spring back to its initial position after meeting an obstacle or enemy, pulling them to the user.

Keep in mind that the distortion can carry debris from surfaces near it to deal higher damage, will track airborne ragdolled enemies, and can sometimes hit the user instead. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 1 Value=5 for distortion, +5 with debris |Stat 2=COOLDOWN |Stat 2 Value=12s |Image=SkyDistortionTemper.gif}} {{Ability |Name='''Turbulence''' |Semi Blockable=y |Interruptible=y |Bypasses Ragdoll=y |Swarm=y |Description=The user grabs the floor beneath them and lifts it like a sheet, resulting in a wave traveling 60 studs to lift any enemy in its way and launch them towards the user.

Keep in mind that the wave cannot be blocked while traveling its first 18 studs, and can be steered since it will follow the user's orientation at all times. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 1 Value=10 |Stat 2=COOLDOWN |Stat 2 Value=15s |Image=Turbulence.gif}} {{Ability |Type=AIR VARIANT |Type Color=red |Name='''Turbulence''' |Semi Blockable=y |Interruptible=y |Semi Ragdoll=y |Melee=y |Explosion=y |Description=If the user was airborne or holding the jump button, they will lift their legs upwards to dropkick upwards rather than downwards, before moving 20 studs into the air then gaining free horizontal flight as they flip around to aim an uncounterable distortion into the ground that will bounce any enemy it hits. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 1 Value=14, 5 for kick, 9 for distortion |Stat 2=COOLDOWN |Stat 2 Value=15s |Image=TurbulenceAir.gif}} {{Ability |Type=HIGH AIR VARIANT |Type Color=red |Name='''Turbulence''' |Blockable=y |Interruptible=y |Bypasses Ragdoll=y |Melee=y |Description=If the user is 25 studs or higher from the ground, their kick will be much fiercer, but won't be followed up by a distortion attack. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 1 Value=8 |Stat 2=COOLDOWN |Stat 2 Value=15s |Image=TurbulenceAir2.gif}} {{Ability |Type=SPECIAL VARIANT / MELEE COUNTER |Type Color=blue |Name='''Turbulence''' |Interruptible=y |Explosion=y |Description=While invisible with Sky Veil, using Turbulence will immediately cancel the invisibility and reveal the user upside down. If hit by a melee attack during this, they will proceed to send a distortion towards their assailant to send them flying away. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 1 Value=12 |Stat 2=COUNTER WINDOW |Stat 2 Value=0.75s |Stat 3=COOLDOWN |Stat 3 Value=15s |Image=TurbulenceSpecial.gif}} {{Ability |Name='''Thin Ice Breaker''' |Unblockable=y |Interruptible=y |Semi Ragdoll=y |Melee=y |Melee Armor=y |Description=The user puts both their hands forwards to strike the surface layer of the sky then shatter it like thin ice, gaining melee i-frames after half a second. The initial part of the skill cannot bypass ragdoll, but is able to stun and grab a single opponent while the user breaks the distortion.

If an airborne ragdolled target is in range, the user will immediately hover to them and ensure that the grab lands, but if the target evades out of the move's ragdoll while above 25 studs of altitude, they will automatically perform the air combo's counterattack. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 1 Value=14, 7 for grab, 7 for shatter |Stat 2=COOLDOWN |Stat 2 Value=15s |Image=ThinIceBreaker.gif}} {{Ability |Type=VARIANT |Type Color=red |Name='''Thin Ice Breaker''' |Unblockable=y |Interruptible=y |Semi Ragdoll=y |Melee=y |Melee Armor=y |Description=While in Temper, the user increases the output of their extension technique, which greatly expands the size, thus range, of their attack. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 1 Value=14, 7 on contact, 7 for shatter |Stat 2=COOLDOWN |Stat 2 Value=15s |Image=ThinIceBreakerTemper.gif}} |-|Awakening Move= {{Ability |Type=AWAKENING ATTACK |Type Color=navy |Name='''Temper''' |Unblockable=y |Uninterruptible=y |Bypasses Ragdoll=y |No Evasive=y |Swarm=y |Explosion=y |Description=The user will fly upwards and begin manipulating a giant distortion, before striking it to unleash a giant shockwave that will eradicate everything within a 50 stud radius and yelling “Don’t act like you won!”.

This awakening can only be used while in Temper, and will end the state immediately. Its damage will be primarily swarm, yet the attack also has an explosion hitbox. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 1 Value=80 |Stat 2=HEALING |Stat 2 Value=25 HP |Stat 3=AWAKENING REFUND |Image=TemperVariant.gif}} |-|Finishers= {{Ability |Name='''Blind Rage''' |Interruptible=y |Melee=y |Description=The user grabs the opponent horizontally and brutally rips them into 2 pieces as they scream in pain, before tossing their parts away. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 1 Value=8 for split, 20 for toss |Stat 2=COOLDOWN |Stat 2 Value=15s |Image=BlindRageFinisher.gif}} {{Ability |Type=AIR VARIANT |Type Color=red |Name='''Turbulence''' |Semi Blockable=y |Interruptible=y |Bypasses Ragdoll=y |Description=The distortion splatters the target's body entirely, leaving nothing behind but a puddle of blood. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 1 Value=Insta-kill |Stat 2=COOLDOWN |Stat 2 Value=15s |Image=TurbulenceFinisher.gif}} {{Ability |Name='''Thin Ice Breaker''' |Unblockable=y |Interruptible=y |Bypasses Ragdoll=y |Melee=y |Description=The user intensifies their surface strike with it having inverted colours while shouting "宇守羅彈" (pronounced: Usurabi, meaning "Thin Ice Breaker"), launching the opponent even farther. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 1 Value=Insta-kill |Stat 2=COOLDOWN |Stat 2 Value=15s |Image=ThinIceBreakerFinisher.gif}} {{Ability |Type=AWAKENING ATTACK |Type Color=navy |Name='''Temper''' |Unblockable=y |Uninterruptible=y |Bypasses Ragdoll=y |No Evasive=y |Swarm=y |Description=The large thin ice breaker crushes all that lies on the surface, splitting enemies into pieces. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 1 Value=Insta-kill |Stat 2=HEALING |Stat 2 Value=25 HP |Image=TemperVariantFinisher.gif}} ==Pros & Cons== {{ProsCons |pros= *Low cooldowns in general. *Can avoid evasion punishes by comboing midair and avoiding M1s. *Decent combo starters, especially while in Temper. *Temper heals regardless of success and can fit into several combos. |cons= *Can struggle with passive players outside of Temper due to the lack of safe block breakers. *Unsafe air combos due to the high damage taken if the opponent evades. *Temper's activation is both interruptible and limited due to its automatic depletion if no damage is dealt. *While in Temper, Blind Rage's first two swings often cause the player to miss the grab, leaving them open to an easy punish. *Temper Thin Ice Breaker is easy to avoid if not properly comboed into. }} ==Combos== {{Combo |sequence1=3 M1s Uppercut + Turbulence (Air) + Sky Distortion + 3 M1s Downslam + Blind Rage + 2 M1s + Thin Ice Breaker |damage1=71 |notes1=Timing Sky Distortion after Turbulence grants enough time for the 2nd M1 and a downslam to hit, which could then be followed by Blind Rage on wake up to set for a quick air combo. Adding another air M1 is risky due to the sudden counterattack from the final skill. |sequence2=3 M1s + Blind Rage + 3 M1s + Turbulence + Thin Ice Breaker + 4 M1s |damage2=75 |notes2=A Temper combo which requires a delay after Blind Rage to get an air M1 reset, then the use of Turbulence and Thin Ice Breaker to supply M1s with time to reset once again. Sky Distortion can be used instead of the 4th M1, but it'd be a waste of a good tool for 1 extra damage. |sequence3=3 M1 Uppercut + Sky Distortion + Thin Ice Breaker + Blind Rage + Turbulence (High Air) + 2 M1s |damage3=58 |notes3=After immediately pressing Sky Distortion when the uppercut lands, you must tilt your camera to the sky, so Thin Ice Breaker would keep them in your range to land Blind Rage. Aside of the Blind Rage timing, this combo lacks any, making it easy to land. }} ==Tips & Techs== ===Tips=== *When using Temper and then using Blind Rage, there are times where you need to aim backwards as the first 2 punches can cause you to miss the grab. *Turbulence and Thin Ice Breaker both launch the target enough to do small air combos. This includes using aerial M1s after the ground variant of Thin Ice Breaker for unpunishable extra damage. ===Techs=== |-|Beginner= ==='''Quickveil'''=== The player can unveil without endlag by pressing an ability that is on cooldown during Sky Veil, allowing for surprise attacks with M1s or dashes. |-|Intermediate= ===='''Double Airslam'''==== By flying directly upwards with Blind Rage without Temper, the extra height allows the player to use an aerial M1 and Thin Ice Breaker before the enemy hits the ground, resetting the player's M1s and allowing for another aerial M1. ===='''Ignored Evasive'''==== By flying directly upwards with Blind Rage, if the enemy uses evasive then the player can block it and use Thin Ice Breaker before hitting the ground due to the extra height. The player can then use aerial M1s or continue the air combo in any way. This can be risky against experienced players since they can delay their evasive to stop you from using Thin Ice Breaker before they hit the ground. |-|Advanced= ==Trivia== *{{Sky Bender}} used to be the first character ever to have 80 HP, although this was shadow-changed after {{V|1.82}}. **It is also the second character to ever be both a base only and Early Access, right after {{Crow Charmer}}. ***And finally, {{Sky Bender}} is the third character that is based on a female Jujutsu Kaisen character, with the first two being {{Star Rage}} and {{Crow Charmer}}. *{{Sky Bender}}'s title used to be "Sky Assassin" before {{V|1.84}}, where it was changed to avoid keyword restrictions in Vietnam from getting ''Jujutsu Shenanigans'' taken down. **The change was initially going to be "Sky Scraper", but was scrapped immediately. *The finishers for Blind Rage and Thin Ice Breaker have a chance to fail and keep the enemy alive. *While in Temper, the user will switch to their equipped Awakening Outfit until the state concludes. **This sets {{Sky Bender}} as the fourth base-only character to be able to benefit from the [[Gamepasses|Awakening Outfit gamepass]], the others being {{Aspiring Mangaka}}, {{Crow Charmer}} and {{Black Death}}. *Temper can still be activated when Awakenings are disabled through the [[Private_Servers#Private_Server_Settings|PS+ settings]] as it is not an actual Awakening. ==Gallery== File:TakakoUro.png|Uro Takako, the inspiration for Sky Bender. ==History== To read about all of the character's changes, expand the collapsible below.
*'''[+]''' : Buff or late addition (after release.) *'''[-]''' : Nerf. *'''[/]''' : Bug fix, miscellanous change.. (does not affect combat in a major way.) {|class="fandom-table" !Update !Additions/Changes/Fixes |- |{{V|1.84}} (extra) | *[/] Changed title from Sky Assassin to Sky Bender. |- |{{V|1.84}} | *[/] Fixed being able to hit airborne standing enemies with the second M1. *[/] Fixed skills being unavailable and added missing animations to Skill Builder. |- |{{V|1.83}} | *[+] Increased Thin Ice Breaker's hitbox size, damage per hit from 5 to 7, and its shatter part now launches the enemy higher. *[+] Decreased Sky Distortion's endlag when hitting a blocking enemy while on the ground. *[+] Air Sky Distortion now moves the user slightly forward at the start. *[-] Increased the combo reset time for aerial M1s. *[-] The second melee attack now knocks downwards instead of to the left during non-Temper air combos. *[-] Reduced Blind Rage's linger duration. *[-] Blind Rage no longer deals damage when crashing through walls. *[-] Blind Rage no longer cancels ragdoll early. *[-] Reduced the damage of Blind Rage's toss from 5 to 4. *[-] Blind Rage and Thin Ice Breaker can no longer hit grounded ragdolls. *[-] Sky Distortion no longer keeps the user in the air if missed. *[-] Temper Sky Distortion now pulls the enemy towards the starting location. *[-] Reduced the damage of Sky Distortion from 12 to 10. *[-] Temper no longer grants i-frames at the very start. *[-] Temper now resets cooldowns to a minimum of 3s. *[/] Released to the public. *[/] Added a new skill: Turbulence. *[/] Added a new special: Sky Veil. *[/] Added a new finisher to Blind Rage. *[/] Added a new Temper variant to Thin Ice Breaker. *[/] Improved the visual and sound effects of certain skills. |- |{{V|1.82}} (extra) | *[+] Increased Max HP from 80 to 100. (unmentioned) *[-] Reduced the damage of Blind Rage's crashes from 5 to 3. *[-] Temper will now drain if the user didn't deal any damage after a certain amount of time. (unmentioned) *[/] Changed M1 trail and bar colors. |- |{{V|1.82}} | *[/] Added as Early Access. *[/] Added a new Awakening: Temper. *[/] Added 3 new moves: Blind Rage, Sky Distortion, Thin Ice Breaker. |}

Kogane.text: {{DISPLAYTITLE:Kogane}} {{Character2 |title1=Kogane |image1= KoganeIcon.jpg|Kogane Johnpetting.gif|Pet LeaderboardKogane.png|Leaderboard Leaderboardicon.jpg|Shenanigans Playlist.png|Playlist }} {{Quote|You have earned five points for a kill.|Kogane}} ==Description== '''Kogane''' is a feature added in {{Update|1.83}}, available to all players. It can be accessed by going to the emote slot, residing next to the right of the emote wheel. [[File:KoganeWheel.png|center|frameless|150px]] When opening Kogane's wheel, four options present themselves: *'''''Emotes''''': Opens the user's emote wheel. *'''''Pet''''': Makes the user pet the Kogane, rewarding them with $5. This reward can only be claimed once per day and increases by $1 for each consecutive day it is collected, up to a maximum of $15. *'''''Leaderboard''''': Pulls up a leaderboard revealing all of the players in the servers, their points, current Elo in Ranked Duels, and achievement completion progress. *'''''Shenanigans''''': Displays a set of options that can be activated using points. Points are gained by killing players in public servers only, but reset to 0 after leaving one. *'''Playlist:''' Gives the user the ability to play music '''only''' while fighting in the game. Music can be tinkered with on the top of the playlist to fit certain needs. **'''Enabled''': Enables the combat music. **'''I + NPCS:''' NPC's count towards combat music. **'''Swap:''' Plays the enemies playlist instead of yours. **'''Time:''' Lets you set the time after the last hit before the song ends. ===Shenanigans=== Shenanigans are modifiers that alter certain rules of ''Jujutsu Shenanigans'' to grant an advantage for whoever picks them: {|class="wikitable" !Shenanigans !Point Cost !In-Game Description !Visual |- |Transfer |5 points |Drop 5 points on the ground. Whoever walks over the points will collect and obtain them. |[[File:Transferingpoints.gif|right|200px]] |- |Revenge |25 points |After dying, you will respawn at the last place you died. |[[File:KoganePointItem1.gif|right|200px]] |- |Void Strider |25 points |When falling off of the void, Haba will fly over and lift you up by hanging a thread on your leg. He will then fly over to the middle of the map and let you go. |[[File:VoidJump.gif|right|200px]] |- |Steed |50 points |Spawns a horse that can be ridden. Unlike Jeeps, the horse will pick up speed the longer it runs for. |[[File:Steelballrunnnn.gif|right|200px]] |- |Liquidation |100 points |Delivers a certain amount of items to you, equivalent to how many players are in the server at that moment. |[[File:Buyingiteems.gif|right|200px]] |- |Nightmare |100 points |Force the sun to go down. |[[File:Nightmaretime.gif|right|200px]] |- |Sunrise |100 points |Force the sun to rise up. |TO BE ADDED |- |Overproduction |100 points |Deliver the closest item to you (0.5x players in the server). |[[File:Itemcopying.gif|right|200px]] |} ===Skins=== In {{Update|V1.84}}, '''Skins''' were added to Jujutsu Shenanigans. Some were given to various [[Characters]] including {{Mahoraga}} and {{Puppet Master}}, but a majority were given to Kogane. File:KoganeWitchHat.png|Kogane's Witch Hat Skin. ==Trivia== *If you begin a message in chat with "Kogane" (capitalization does not matter), Kogane will respond with a random message, those being: "No!!", "No!!! Never!!!", "Yes!!", "Yes!!! of course!!", "Maybe..", "Can you repeat that? huh??", "GENERATING RESPONSE... UNLICENSED GPT ERROR!", "Pay me to find out", "Do not even dare" *Sending a message that reads "Yo Kogane" (Case sensitive) in chat will make Kogane always respond with "Wassup (hey yumi where's my voice)", the part in parentheses most likely being an inside joke with a head mod of JJS, Yumiseal, and the dev team. ** If you send that same message but without a capital Y at the beginning of 'Yo', Kogane has a larger pool of responses, those responses being: "Hello!!!", "how can i help ya?", "What", "yelloooooo", "hello!!???", "hi", "hi im kogane", "Wassup (hey yumi where's my voice)", "Konichiwhatsup", "loser says what", "hi that's my name", "yo, gurt !!", and "Sorry I don't respond to fools". *Kogane will disappear after a short time with no interaction, and will be visibly sad when its corresponding player dies during its presence. *Kogane was originally going to be an emote, but had several bumps during its development before it was changed to be a feature. *Kogane can still respond to chat commands even if they were filtered by Roblox. ==Gallery== File:ReferenceKogane.png|Kogane's look in the Jujutsu Kaisen series. [[Category:Characters]][[Category:Complete_Characters]] {{DISPLAYTITLE:'''Vessel'''}} (Not to be confused with the "Vessel" and "VESSELLL" [[emotes]]) {{Character2 |title1={{Vessel}} |cost=Free |awakening='''King Of Curses''' |special= *'''Combat Instincts''' *'''Cleave''' |hp=85 |image1= Vessel.png|Base Vessel awakening.png|Awakening |previous={{Honored One}} |next={{The Fallen}}}} {{Quote|I'll accept it Mahito. I am you.|Yuji Itadori ({{Vessel}}) to Mahito ({{Perfection}})}} ==Description== '''Vessel''' is one of the three first [[Characters]] added into ''Jujutsu Shenanigans'' along with {{Honored One}} and {{Restless Gambler}}. ===Origin=== {{Origin|Vessel is based off of Yuji Itadori and Ryomen Sukuna, characters from ''Jujutsu Kaisen''.|{{JJK|Yuji Itadori}} serves as ''Jujutsu Kaisen'''s central protagonist. Before becoming a jujutsu sorcerer, Yuji was living a relatively normal life until he ate a cursed finger belonging to {{JJK|Ryomen Sukuna}}, one of the main antagonists of the series. This caused the King of Curses to reincarnate and possess Yuji's body, hence the title: "Vessel".}} ==Moveset== |-|Base= {{Ability |Type=SPECIAL |Type Color=orange |Interruptible=y |Name='''Combat Instincts''' |Description=Using the special during an M1 or a skill's windup (excluding Manji Kick) immediately cancels the attack with no endlag, while also keeping the move off cooldown. Although this is mainly used to bait enemies into blocking or using a counter, this can notably be used with aerial variants as well to gain height or mobility. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 1 Value=None |Stat 2=AWAKENING COST |Stat 2 Value=3% (unrequired) |Stat 3=COOLDOWN |Stat 3 Value=2s |Image=CombatInstincts.gif}} {{Ability |Type=SPECIAL VARIANT |Type Color=orange |Unblockable=y |Interruptible=y |Bypasses Ragdoll=y |Bullet=y |Name='''Combat Instincts''' |Description=Triggering the special while standing near a throwable will make the user throw a punch that hurls the throwable forward. Unlike the normal special, this variant requires Awakening meter. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 1 Value=15 from throwables |Stat 2=AWAKENING COST |Stat 2 Value=3% |Stat 3=COOLDOWN |Stat 3 Value=2s |Image=CombatInstinctsThrow.gif}} {{Ability |360 Blockable=y |Cannot Bypass Ragdoll=y |Melee=y |Bullet Armor=y |Name='''Cursed Strikes''' |Description=The user swiftly slides forward with their hands poised to attack as their eyes glow in red. If they meet an opponent, the user will gain bullet i-frames as they release a flurry of punches, finished with a right calf kick that leaves the target stunned in place.

After the attack is over, the user's M1 count will be saved and their front dash will be disabled for a moment. If blocked however, the user's slide will be cut short. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 1 Value=17.5 in total, 4 on grab, 1.75 per punch (x6), 3 for kick |Stat 2=COOLDOWN |Stat 2 Value=14s |Image=CursedStrikes.gif}} {{Ability |Type=AIR VARIANT |Type Color=red |Unblockable=y |Interruptible=y |Bypasses Ragdoll=y |No Lock On=y |Melee=y |Name='''Cursed Strikes''' |Description=If the user was airborne, they will instead launch themselves toward the ground with a powerful cursed-energy infused dropkick, grounding whoever they land on. The attack cannot be directly aimed downwards nor can it be feinted after the preparation hop. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 1 Value=14 |Stat 2=COOLDOWN |Stat 2 Value=14s |Image=CursedStrikesAir.gif}} {{Ability |Name='''Crushing Blow''' |Unblockable=y |Bypasses Ragdoll=y |Interruptible=y |Melee=y |Description=The user charges cursed energy in their hand while getting ready to slam the floor. If a target is near, they shall be grabbed by the torso and slammed into the ground twice, then launched in the sky as the user lets go. If the move doesn't hit any target, the initial hit will release a shockwave with lower damage. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 1 Value=12 in total, 6 per slam (x2), 3 for miss shockwave |Stat 2=COOLDOWN |Stat 2 Value=15s |Image=CrushingBlow.gif}} {{Ability |Type=AIR VARIANT |Type Color=red |360 Blockable=y |Bypasses Ragdoll=y |Interruptible=y |Melee=y |Name='''Crushing Blow''' |Description=With their fist imbued with cursed energy, the user dashes across the air, grabs the enemy, and performs the same attack. Feinting this move allows the user to take advantage of the initial hop, offering advantageous mobility. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 1 Value=12 in total, 6 per slam (x2), 3 for miss shockwave |Stat 2=COOLDOWN |Stat 2 Value=15s |Image=CrushingBlowAir.gif}} {{Ability |Semi Blockable=y |Interruptible=y |Semi Ragdoll=y |Melee=y |Name='''Divergent Fist''' |Description=The user winds their arm back and lands a decent blow with their fist before delayed cursed energy launches the opponent back. |Stat 2=COOLDOWN |Stat 2 Value=40s |Image=OpenFinisher.gif}} ==Pros & Cons== {{ProsCons |pros= *Their simple combos with moves that flow together can easily grant an impressive damage output. *Every single move (if not the base, then the variant) can break block, bypass ragdoll, and damage domains with the exception of Manji Kick. *Cursed Strikes is a very effective true combo extender with a variant that can be used to finish off enemies or bait out their counters/ragdoll cancels when paired with Combat Instincts. *Feinting can be done freely, as it does not require any Awakening meter despite using it up when available, all while operating on a fairly short cooldown. *Excels in close combat due to passives in both base and Awakening, allowing the user to either win most M1 trades or keep enemies away with ranged slashes. *Compensates for the lack of range in base by utilizing abilities like Open, Rush, and Aerial Dismantle while in Awakening. *Incredibly tough to take down in awakening due to long M1's and an incredible heal upon using it. *Malevolent Shrine puts intense pressure on enemies by eating away at their health and is nigh-inescapable. |cons= *All base moves are melee, meaning they lack range, are susceptible to counters, are primarily only good when confirmed off of M1s, and can often be punished by ragdoll cancels when landing. *85 Max HP, which is lower than most characters in the game. *Feinting moves for mobility can be punished and interrupted if done predictably. *Chaining Black Flashes is inconsistent and can usually only be done on opponents with high ping or poor reaction times. *Open can easily be dodged in broad spaces. *World Cutting Slash has a lengthy startup and cooldown, meaning it can be easily canceled or dodged by a prepared opponent. }} ==Combos== |-|Base= {{Combos |sequence1=M1 + Cursed Strikes + 3 M1s + Crushing Blow |damage1=42.5 |notes1=A simple yet unevadable combo, using Cursed Strikes after the first M1 to yield the highest true damage possible (chaining excluded). |sequence2=3 M1s Uppercut + Crushing Blow + Cursed Strikes + 3 M1s + Divergent Fist (Black Flash Chain) |damage2=63.5 - 89.5 |notes2=Crushing This lets it M1 reset in order for Crushing Blow's air ragdoll to be utilized in landing a regular M1 along with a true downslam. |sequence4=Manji Kick + Crushing Blow + Cursed Strikes + 3 M1s + Divergent Fist (Black Flash Chain) |damage4=58 - 83 |notes4=You can confirm Crushing Blow after a successful Manji Kick, then you M1 reset with Cursed Strikes then follow up with a Black Flash chain. }} |-|Awakening= {{Combos |sequence1=4 M1s + Dismantle + 3 M1s + Cleave + Rush |damage1=89.9 |notes1=N/A |sequence2=Open + Rush + Dismantle (Air Variant) |damage2=80 |notes2=Be careful on timing Rush after Open |sequence3=3 M1 + Cleave + Side Dash + Dismantle + 3 M1s + Rush |damage3=98.5 |notes3=Potentially a one-shot combo if you add a Front Dash }} ==Tips & Techs== ===Tips=== *Using Cursed Strikes, Crushing Blow, or Manji Kick while in a Black Flash chain will put Divergent Fist on cooldown, the same happens if the player start another one and feint it with R and then use any other move, even feinting Cursed Strikes or Crushing Blow puts it on cooldown. This is unless they feint the last black flash. *In Malevolent Shrine, another way to break the block of trapped enemies is by utilizing the front dash to hit their back. Be mindful that the front dash, Rush, and Cleave can only work on one person at a time (or more if they are cramped together), so using Open, World Cutting Slash, or Aerial Dismantle is generally more effective for groups caught within the domain. *Divergent Fist and Aerial Cursed Strikes are punishable with ragdoll cancel if landed. Therefore, it is advised to only use these moves after baiting it. *Open is a better confirm into Malevolent Shrine than the 4th M1 as it has a longer ragdoll duration, although the player still has to bait evasive. ===Techs=== |-|Beginner= ===={{WdsTooltips |toggle = {{{basic-tooltip|'''Crushing Strikes'''}}} |content = [[File:CrushingStrikesDemonstration.gif|frameless|240x240px]]}}==== The player can catch enemies in the air with Cursed Strikes after landing a Crushing Blow, allowing them to extend your combo with the basic attack when the move ends as your M1 count resets. This tech isn't always safe as Crushing Blow often tends to keep the enemy under rubble. ===={{WdsTooltips |toggle = {{{basic-tooltip|'''World Confirmed Slash'''}}} |content = [[File:GuaranteedWCSDemonstration.gif|frameless|240x240px]]}}==== After landing a point-blank Open, the player has enough time to chant their World Cutting Slash and finish the enemy, assuming they don't have ragdoll cancel to act against them before the chant. |-|Intermediate= ===={{WdsTooltips |toggle = {{{basic-tooltip|'''Crushing Flash'''}}} |content = [[File:CrushingFlash.gif|frameless|240x240px]]}}==== Additionally, it's also possible to hit an opponent with Black Flash following a Crushing Blow. This is done by jumping and using Black Flash as you rise. ===='''Cursed M1 Reset'''==== Requires near perfect timing to pull off. for this technique you need to use your first move within the few frames after the first m1. It allows for a slight increase in all combo damage due to having an extra m1 from the start. |-|Advanced= After landing a successful Manji Kick you can use Cursed Strikes at a specific moment for a red combo extender. Note that you can also do this after a Black Flash or Divergent Fist. ---- ==Trivia== *{{Vessel}} is the first character to be based on 2 ''Jujutsu Kaisen'' characters at once, the others being {{Cursed Partners}}, {{Crow Charmer}}, and {{Switcher}}. *Initially, {{Vessel}}'s Awakening color was blue, with its name being '''Sukuna'''. *{{Vessel}} had several scrapped base moves and a special in the early stages of its development: Cursed Punches, Slaughter Demon, Survival Knife, Cranium Smash, Triple Kick, and Cursed Charge. The special used to be Divergent Fist, which cost 10% Awakening progress to use **Crushing Blow used to also be different, as it was a ranged move where the user would pick up debris and toss it, similarly to {{Mahoraga}}'s Ground Pitch. *There used to be another Black Flash that {{Vessel}} could preform that was activated by perfect blocking, and then immediately punching. '''{{Mahoraga}}'s''' ritual plays the same soundtrack, but it ends early once the shikigami is fully summoned. *{{Vessel}}'s [[Events#April_Fools_2026_Event|2026 April Fools]] name (red judas) is based on the '''[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Gaga Lady Gaga]''' song, [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9WfWnkVLwao Judas]. **The name was chosen due to a multitude of animations and edits of {{JJK|Satoru Gojo vs. Sukuna|The Battle Of The Strongest}} using the song, eventually devolving into {{Honored One}} and {{Vessel}} being called '''blue judas''' and '''red judas''' respectively. *The art of Unlicensed Rhythm Game's "Pass On" shows {{Vessel}} taking the place of Sinclair from Limbus Company. **They are shown next to {{Restless Gambler}} in front of {{Head of the Hei}}, showing a menu of food. ==Gallery== File:Itadori Yuji.png|Yuji Itadori, the inspiration for Vessel's base. Before that, update info was clumped together. '''''We've made sure to apply that change to all updates before V1.57 for consistency and better readability.''''' **'''V1.57''' featured another change to the update log interface, this time detailing the update's contents based on the game's current features, characters, gamemodes, and bugs. '''''This new format will only be applied to subsequent updates, not the ones before V1.57.''''' *At times, special updates get unique titles instead of the usual "The '''''NOTHING''''' Update": **'''{{V|1.00}}''' was titled {{WdsTooltips|toggle = {{{basic-tooltip|"The '''''CHANGELOG''''' Update"}}}|content = [[File:Update.png|frameless|240x240px]]}}, because it only had one note, repeated five times: "Added a changelog". **'''{{V|1.50}}''' was titled "The '''''50TH''''' Update". **'''{{V|1.53}}''' was titled "The '''''EVERYTHING''''' Update", due to being released during April 1st 2025, a day which marks the game's one year anniversary, along with April Fools. **'''{{V|1.67}}''' was titled "The '''👀''' Update", a nod to the "6-7" meme. **'''{{V|1.75}}''' was titled "The '''''SOMETHING''''' Update, Part 2", as it was released during April 1st 2026, a day which marked the game's two year anniversary. *The game developers love to withold certain added features or even buffs/nerfs to a specific character to let the community find out about them.

everyone under it, causing them to splatter to pieces due to the immense pressure. |Stat 1=DAMAGE |Stat 1 Value=Insta-kill |Stat 2=COOLDOWN |Stat 2 Value=25s |Image=MaxElephantFinisher.gif}} ==Pros & Cons== {{ProsCons|pros= *Fast strategic base moveset, with high damage, mobility and strong neutral tools. *Rabbit Escape and Divine Dog: Totality place high pressure on the enemy and forces them to hold block. *Nue is one of the safest evasive bait tools in the game due to its fast tracking from a safe distance, along with how it can set up into Toad or a downslam. *Can perform near oneshot combos while awakened due to possessing a total of 7 different attacks. |cons= *Lower Max HP. *Several moves become unsafe when in close range or without baiting ragdoll cancel. *Long cooldowns and startups for many base & Awakening moves. *Rabbit Escape can be interrupted by any ranged character even after the rabbits land, while Divine Dog: Totality gets nullified by passive play due to it being blockable from all sides. }} ==Combos== |-|Base= {{Combos |sequence1=3 M1s Uppercut + Divine Dog: Totality + Toad + 3 M1s Downslam + Divine Dog: Totality + Nue + Rabbit Escape + Divine Dog: Totality |damage1=74 |notes1=This combo requires summoning the Divine Dog beforehand }} |-|Awakening= {{Combos |sequence1=Awakening + 4 M1s + Well Unknown Abyss + Rabbit Escape + Switch + Great Serpent + Switch + Nue + Switch + Max Elephant + Shadow Swarm |damage1=138 |notes1=N/A }} ==Tips & Techs== ===Tips=== *Throwing an item while using Lurking Shadow (such as a Bowling Ball or Hazenoki's Eye) will make it so the item is automatically used the next time you enter the shadows. *Your best confirm into Toad or its variant out of M1s is by uppercutting. However, this isn't recommended if your opponent still has their evasive, as it's easily punishable when blocked. Nue is a viable option, but the window to use Toad after it is quite short and forces you to predict if the winged shikigami will land. *Chimera Shadow Garden does not affect 0.2 Domain, Idle Death Gamble, Deadly Sentencing, Authentic Mutual Love and Incomplete Shrine's sure-hit effects as the domains either have no sure-hit effects to disable or lack borders entirely. **Chimera Shadow Garden will keep draining health despite Deadly Sentencing's immunity. It's best to just close the domain and summon Mahoraga as nobody will be able to cancel it. *Since {{Mahoraga}} is technically its own character, and a third entity and doesn't require a certain amount of awakening process, you can use it to "heal" yourself to full while in a tough spot. **In Duels, summoning Mahoraga will take away a life. ===Techs=== |-|Beginner= ===={{WdsTooltips |toggle = {{{basic-tooltip|'''Max Rabbit'''}}} |content = [[File:MaxRabbit.gif|frameless|600x338px]]}}==== Before aiming to use Max Elephant, you should use Rabbit Escape on the target as they won't be able to move and rush you, nor dash away to run, giving you a good window to aim Max Elephant. Additionally, this can be used to guarantee any Awakening move except for Mahoraga but even then, it gives you a safe window for some time during the wind-up. |-|Intermediate= ===={{WdsTooltips |toggle = {{{basic-tooltip|'''Great Ritual'''}}} |content = [[File:AerialRitual.gif|frameless|600x338px]]}}==== When landing Great Serpent on an enemy, you can direct it diagonally upwards for 5 seconds. This provides enough time to which even if the enemy does have their ragdoll cancel, you still can successfully summon Mahoraga. The enemy will not have enough time to interrupt it. ===={{WdsTooltips |toggle = {{{basic-tooltip|'''Rabbit Suspension'''}}} |content = [[File:RabbitSuspension.gif|frameless|600x338px]]}}==== Rabbit Escape not only suspends grounded enemies, but also airborne targets. Uppercutting into a Divine Dog attack and following up with Rabbit Escape will suspend the target in the air and make sure all rabbits hit properly without ending the combo. On top of that, jumping and landing an M1 while the target is falling down will ensure that its stun carries over, confirming the rest of the M1 set. |-|Advanced= ===={{WdsTooltips |toggle = {{{basic-tooltip|'''Suspension Ritual'''}}} |content = [[File:SuspendedRitual.gif|frameless|600x338px]]}}==== After killing an enemy, you have an extremely tiny window to start the Mahoraga ritual with their corpse. If you're too late, Mahoraga will not spawn behind you and you will lose most of you Awakening. While this is very useful in Ranked, it is risky, and you will forfeit a life after summoning Mahoraga. ==Trivia== *Emoting while Divine Dog: Totality is summoned will make it do the "Dogsync" emote with you, and it will stop only once you do. **When you summon Mahoraga and still have your Divine Dog standing beside you, it will not despawn. However, it cannot be commanded and will despawn once you get ragdolled. *Rabbit Escape's shikigami have a texture of a meme with a rabbit saying "Nah, I'd win" on their faces. Additionally, Toad has the same text on its eyes. **This texture does not show up on either move's variant. *{{Ten Shadows}}'s [[Events#April_Fools_2026_Event|2026 April Fools]] Name (potential man) is based off of a meme of Megumi having high potential but never uses his potential. *Once '''{{Mahoraga}}''''s ritual successfully starts, '''[https://youtu.be/vxTLtmpnKn8?si=pjbR4YSDNm6OzI5p&t=52 Sukuna vs Mahoraga]''' by '''PHAROZEN''' starts playing. *The art for Unlicensed Rhythm Game's "Pass On" shows {{Ten Shadows}} taking the place of Yi Sang from Limbus Company. ==Gallery== File:Megumi Fushiguro.png|Megumi Fushiguro, the inspiration for the character. File:CSGScrapped.gif|Scrapped "Domain Expansion: Chimera Shadow Garden" move. File:DogsyncDemonstration.gif|Divine Dog performing the "Dogsync" emote. Tips & Techs.text: {{DISPLAYTITLE:'''Tips & Techs'''}} This page dissects how a player can use game features to their advantage. Character specified techs can be found in said [[characters]] page. (W.I.P) ==General Tips== |-|Neutral= *Before every combo, both parties are locked in a "neutral" state. This happens when neither player has advantage over the other, and both must use their offense to breach the other's defense using their neutral tools and start combos. Such interactions may happen at least twice every fight due to ragdoll cancel. *The default method of winning a neutral interaction is M1 trading. In this situation, both parties are exchanging hits and attempting to punish each other's M1 endlag. Ping, reaction speed, and good tracking all play major parts in this, unlike M1 speed passives which rarely makes a difference due to how small the speed difference is between the M1s. **Front dashes are an optimal choice, but are unreliable as they can be easily telegraphed. *A good example of move that functions as a neutral tool is {{Black Death}}'s Chokehold, as it is a powerful attack that allows them to punish opponents even while attacking or blocking; forcing the opponent to think carefully about how they approach, lest they get grabbed by the move. |-|M1 Catching= *Several abilities can serve as mobility tools to close the gap and start M1 trades, including dashes as well. However, these abilities commonly lack armor. This technically opens a window for the enemy to interrupt the movement and start a combo. *For example, take instance of the altitude from a feinted Aerial Cursed Strikes. While it can bait counters, some players will instead choose to immediately forward dash and catch you mid-air to start a combo. It's important to read a player's movements beforehand, or to avoid using mobility moves at a distance where the enemy is able to interrupt you. |-|Ragdoll Cancel= ===Usage=== *Ragdoll cancel is a valuable resource in fights, and being without it will leave you vulnerable to long combos. Being baited to dashing away from the enemy the moment you're ragdolled is a really good way to waste it. *Instead, it is recommended to dash into the enemy while holding the M1 button when they are about to use/have used an attack with a severely long windup/endlag to easily capitalize off of it and punish them. ===Baiting=== *Uncommonly, some players refuse to use ragdoll cancel when ragdolled. This often is because they have not found a window to punish you, and are waiting for your next move in order to punish it. While aware of this, you may be pressured into doing shorter combos and resetting back to neutral, losing out on damage. However, there are few ways to force ragdoll cancel. **Using a move that disables ragdoll cancel (Nue, Fluttering Pounce's air combo..) can allow you to extend from a safe distance and thus forces the enemy to use their ragdoll cancel during the windup in order to avoid being comboed. **Feinting attacks such as Aerial Cursed Strikes with the special also helps since you'll be avoiding the endlag entirely, but not all characters are able to do so. |-|Burst= *The same strategies with ragdoll cancel also shine with anti-team burst, seeing as it can be used while stunned/still standing (rather than just ragdolled) to punish enemies for even landing an M1, and you are allowed to try again after failing said punish. **Getting attacked by a multi-hit grab move (eg. Rapid Punches and Cursed Strikes) after using burst can turn the tide in a battle against multiple players, as each hit from the attack will restore your evasive. Paired with the attack being unescapable, spamming your dash button will practically trigger several bursts in a row, healing you by a margin. '''(This only works with certain moves now)''' ***Note that this does not work if the evasive was obtained off of interruption, as it can only be used once. Regardless, it is still worth using since said grab moves lose their stun, meaning counters and block are usable while being hit during the grab move (M1s won't work due to the grab moves having melee armor, and other attacks may be interrupted). ==General Techs== |-|Beginner= ===='''Whiffing Forward-Dash'''==== When using Forward Dash to catch enemy, you would notice the huge endlag that would get yourself punished by opponent if that said Forward Dash gets blocked. To avoid this, if you estimate that your Forward-Dash would be blocked by enemy, you can try to do a turn-around while traveling to prevent it from landing on your enemy's block, thus preventing the punishment. ===='''True Downslam'''==== Almost every character has a move where they launch their opponent up. Take this time to start M1ing. Once they fall, you can down slam them, however this gives them more evasive meter. ===='''Wrap Around'''==== An easy and effective way to get around enemy's block is by getting mildly close to your opponent, then using Forward-Dash at them, and then doing the 180 camera flick when your Forward Dash passes the enemy block to hit them from the back, technically bypassing their block. Keep in mind that the enemy would likely avoid this by side-dashing away and running around to hinder the ability to use this tech, or even if this works, the chance is your opponent would be knocked away due to the feature that prevents unfair advantage for lock-on players. |-|Intermediate= ===='''Side-Dashing M1'''==== As like the name of the tech, this involve the user get around the enemy's block by doing Side-dash while M1 at the same time to technically bypass the opponent's block. As for the opposite side, you can try zoning and keep a comfortable distance that wouldn't get you surprised by Side-Dashing M1. ===='''M1 Range Extender'''==== When performing M1s, turning your camera about 20 degrees will slightly extend their effective range. You can use this to catch your opponent off guard with M1s or win M1 trades more easily. This can also be used to perform the Forward-Dash Combo Extender tech. |-|Advanced= ===='''Uppercut Surfing'''==== When holding jump during an M1 chain and delaying the input between your 3rd M1 and your 4th just enough, you can jump on your opponents head whilst doing an uppercut to gain height and increase your opponents ragdoll time. Alternatively, you can do your M1 twice then jump on their head and hold m1 and space bar/jump button for the remainder of your m1 chain. Holding jump after the surf can make you and the opponent go higher in the air. This makes uppercuts near unpunishable, and is especially good for characters like Restless Gambler and Locust Guy, as you can increase the damage of Rough Energy's air variant without needing a Shutter Door to bounce on or a height advantage beforehand, the former, and starting an air combo without using any of your moves, the latter. Do note that this cannot be performed with Head of the Hei, due to them not being able to uppercut. ===='''Getup Theory'''==== (OUTDATED) Landing an M1 or dash the frame someone gets up from ragdoll, allows you to combo ragdoll to M1s without using any moves. Like mentioned, this is frame perfect, but there are moves that allow you to use audio cues or counting to do it semi-consistently with lots of practice. You can abuse this by first uppercutting an enemy, and holding M1 and constantly uppercutting, to start an infinite combo, however, this builds up evasive fast, and is only useful for when your moves are on cooldown or for when you have no moves, due to Defense Attorney's Confiscation or after using all moves twice with the Never Again binding vow. ===='''Forward-Dash Combo Extender'''==== By performing the M1 Range Extend tech and then dashing into your opponent, you can push them just enough to land a front dash without ragdolling them, effectively adding 4 extra damage. This tech can be done on any character (except Head of the Hei). Note that it must be executed correctly and quickly to land, and it will not reset your M1s. ----

His cursed technique, Boogie Woogie, revolves around clapping his hands to switch spots with anything that has a cursed energy level above a certain amount, a technique which he uses very effectively, hence the title: "Switcher". }} ==Moveset== |-|Base= {{Ability |Type=SPECIAL |Type Color=orange |Name='''Boogie Woogie''' |Semi Blockable=y |Bypasses Ragdoll=y |Interruptible=y |No Lock On=y |Description=When using the special on a target within 60 studs, the user claps their hands to activate their cursed technique and instantly swap places and orientations with the target. Precisely, any action the user has inputted during a clap will be executed on the exact moment the clap ends. *Claps can be initiated while dashing, running, or even during a move. Their speed also gets higher the closer the target is to the user, becoming nearly instant when in close range, and even while targeting a ragdolled enemy or feinting a skill. **Initiating a clap during a move will cancel the skill and put it on cooldown. For moves other than Pebble Throw, their cooldown will be halved if the moves were feinted before the actual attack. *The enemy's console lock on will be disabled for 1.5s. *Swaps are blockable from all sides, but become unblockable if the target is within 35 studs of the user. **The special will go on half its cooldown if a swap is blocked. |Stat 1=AWAKENING COST |Stat 1 Value=6% (unrequired) |Stat 2=COOLDOWN |Stat 2 Value=6s, 3s on block |Image=BoogieWoogie.gif}} {{Ability |Type=SPECIAL VARIANT |Type Color=orange |Name='''Boogie Woogie: Item Swap''' |Interruptible=y |Description=On top of being able to swap with people, Boogie Woogie is able to target objects with cursed energy as well.

Swaps cannot be perfected feinting moves or swapping with Pebble Throw's projectile. |Stat 1=AWAKENING COST |Stat 2=COOLDOWN |Stat 2 Value=1-2s (depends on range), 4s on block, none on ragdoll/items |Image=BoogieWoogiePerfectSwap.gif}} {{Ability |Type=SPECIAL VARIANT |Type Color=orange |Name='''Boogie Woogie: Target Swap''' |Semi Blockable=y |Bypasses Ragdoll=y |Interruptible=y |No Lock On=y |Description=The user can also apply their technique to switch between others with a clap by hovering their cursor over two different targets before clapping. Please don't add any combos whatsoever.''''' |notes1=---- }} |-|Awakening= {{Combo |sequence1=---- |damage1='''''This character Combos are currently being reworked.
Please don't add any combos whatsoever.''''' |notes1=---- }} ==Tips & Techs== ===Tips=== *Switching with a player will not only switch between your positions, but also the directions you faced. As most fights have the opponent facing you, you're able to look away right before a swap and get the upperhand, leaving them open for attacks. This can also be used to dodge ranged moves as well, by swapping at the very last second. **This also comes in handy when the target is ragdolled away, as the swap will conserve their momentum and keep them sliding towards you in order to combo extend. *Boogie Woogie is able to be used on {{Puppet Master}}'s Offload puppets, {{Head of the Hei}}'s Flash Freezing, and {{Lucky Coward}}'s Helping Hand. *While feinting moves may seem useless at first, you are able to perform several tricks by using Pebble Throw prior to feinting a move after it has hit: **By using Pebble Throw then tossing an enemy with Swift Kick's first hit towards the lingering projectile, you're able cancel the rest of the move and perform a swap with the pebble to appear near the target, effectively doing a true M1 reset. Note that this interaction can get you punished if the target wasn't ragdolled without evasive prior to using Pebble Throw. **Elbow Drop's initial hit will apply true ragdoll, disabling evasive and letting you follow up with other moves to perform a short true combo. This can also be paired with a lingering pebble to immediately Black Flash the opponent on their way down. *As of {{V|1.43}}, you cannot switch during domain expansions or while above the void unless it is with Pebble Throw's projectile. ===Techs=== |-|Beginner= ===={{WdsTooltips |toggle = {{{basic-tooltip|'''Misswitch'''}}} |content = [[File:Misswitch.gif|frameless|240x240px]]}}==== By looking away before a swap, you can throw off any opponent's incoming attack (works better with ranged moves) to make them miss. You're likely to be looking at them if they were aiming at you, especially if they didn't expect it. You can also use this tech to dash behind opponents. ===={{WdsTooltips |toggle = {{{basic-tooltip|'''Swift Toss'''}}} |content = [[File:SwiftToss.gif|frameless|240x240px]]}}==== As Swift Kick's throw is aimable, you're able to throw an enemy upwards and get the most out of their ragdoll to wind up a downslam. This can be punished heavily if you misstime the hit. |-|Intermediate= ===={{WdsTooltips |toggle = {{{basic-tooltip|'''Dream Flick'''}}} |content = [[File:DreamFlick.gif|frameless|240x240px]]}}==== Dreams can extend a combo and reset your M1s if you miss its last hit and land it on an unragdolled opponent to avoid having to deal with melee stun immunity. |-|Advanced= ===='''Black Flash Drop'''==== Following a Downslam, you can execute a Pebble Throw (intentionally missing) to manipulate the timing. If timed precisely as the opponent begins their wake-up animation, you can land an Elbow Drop and immediately feint it to provide a consistent window to confirm a Black Flash. This combo is mostly flashy, but guarantees true damage if the target is about to regain their evasion. ===={{WdsTooltips |toggle = {{{basic-tooltip|'''Swift Kick M1 Reset'''}}} |content = [[File:Misswitch.gif|frameless|240x240px]]}}==== Following an uppercut, you can use Pebble Throw (intentionally missing) and then use Swift Kick, kicking the enemy further from the pebble, to unragdoll and stun them. Then use Boogie Woogie and steer Blazing Star towards the stunned enemy so you can dash in, resulting in an M1 reset. ==Trivia== *When {{Switcher}} was added, its Awakening was formerly called Memories that didn't exist, before it was changed to False Memories in {{V|1.43}}. *The texture of Pebble Throw's projectile will match the floor that the user is currently standing on. If there is no ground beneath the user, the pebble will be white. **You can enter domains using Pebble Throw by swapping after the pebble goes through the domain's border. **If you use Jeep emote right after pebble throw when you press special, You will swap at your current place. *When reaching a certain airtime with Elbow Drop, an overlay of Choso cutting Todo's hair will cover both your and the target's screens, accompanied by a vine boom. *{{Switcher}} is the first character to be comprised of 3 characters at the same time, those being Aoi Todo, Nobuko Takada, and Itadori Yuji. *{{Switcher}} is also the first of five characters to have non-domain cutscenes (others being {{Aspiring Mangaka}}, {{Salaryman}}, {{Lucky Coward}}, and {{True Cannon}}) *During False Memories, the idol will constantly do the pose from the "Potential2" [[Emotes|emote]]. **During Idol's Debut and Climax Jumping, only the user perceives their idol helping them. From another player's point of view, it's the Switcher himself doing the attacks. **During Dreams, the idol will start doing a sped up version of the "Stylish" [[Emotes|emote]]. **During stun or ragdoll, the idol will disappear. *The music that plays during the Awakening sequence is called [https://youtu.be/67MvFRgX1fw?si=CLa3vQCC4Cx4DRGW HIGHEST☆JUMPING] **The one that plays when using Brute Force's black flash is called [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6UzJNzvAg1g&t=60s Fight Alongside]. The soundtrack will continue playing for a few more seconds if the finisher was landed. **Both OSTs are composed by '''Yoshimasa Terui'''. *{{Switcher}}'s [[Events#April Fools 2026 Event|2026 April Fools]] Name (menace to society) is based off of AniDiscourse's [https://www.youtube.com/shorts/lt6Dubdgp5M "Evil Twin To-do"] short. **These origins are shared with {{Lucky Coward}} (kind scholar), {{Defense Attorney}} (greedy lawyer), {{Blood Manipulator}} (loving and caring brother), {{Perfection}} (purifier) and {{Salaryman}} (enjoys beating the life out of). *The art for "Pass On" during the Unlicensed Rhythm Game shows {{Switcher}} with Aoi Todo's scar, taking the place of Charon from Limbus Company. ==Gallery== File:Switcha.jpeg|Aoi Todo along with his idol, the inspiration for Switcher and its awakening. According to legends, {{Jjk|Ryomen Sukuna}} was an imaginary demon with 4 arms and 2 faces, though in truth he was a human that actually existed during the Heian era.
